# Agent Autoloop

**让你的命令行 Agent 在后台自己接活、自己跟进到底；平时不烦你，遇到拿不准的事才发卡片找你拍板。**

**中文** | [English](README.en.md)

[上手](#上手) · [场景模板](#拿来即用的场景模板) · [插件](#插件体系四个方向都能自由替换) · [内核](#内核的四个机制) · [文档](#更多文档)

架构图

## 它解决什么问题？

平时我们用 Claude Code、Codex 这类命令行 Agent，大多是“人守着终端用”：你输一句话，盯着它跑，等它问你下一步；一旦关掉窗口或者人走开，事情就断了。

**Agent Autoloop** 是一个极轻量的自动化中台。它把任务调度做成一个零外部依赖的**内核**，把事件来源、Agent、通知通道，甚至代码上线流水线全部拆成可随时插拔的**插件**。

- **一台电脑、一条命令就能跑。** 装在你的 Windows、Mac 或 Linux 上，不用买云服务器，也不用开放公网端口。
- **一行配置接新 Agent。** 不需要 SDK，也不需要改 Agent 源码，能接收提示词并打印最后一条回复的命令行工具都能接。
- **没有后台界面。** 需要你拍板时把卡片推到飞书、钉钉、企微、Slack、Discord 或桌面通知；想看全局进展，敲一行命令。

## 上手

支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。需要 Node 24 或更新、Git，以及一个已经登录的命令行 Agent；macOS/Linux 还需要 curl，不需要 GitHub 账号。也可以把[安装说明](INSTALL.md)交给你的 Agent。

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

macOS / Linux：

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/main/install.sh | sh
```

安装和 `agent-autoloop update` 都装最新的 [Release](https://github.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/releases)，那是通过了全部检查的版本。

装好后用你本机的 Agent 真实走一遍“提问 → 退出等回复 → 拍板 → 接着干完”：

```bash
agent-autoloop try
```

下面是在终端里的真实输出：

```text
事件发出去了，Agent 开始干活……

Agent 结束了这一轮，问了你一个问题。它现在不占进程、不花 Token。

【等你决定】#1 试跑：选一个颜色
这是一次试跑，选哪个都行。
  1. 蓝色
  2. 绿色
回答：agent-autoloop answer 1
答完运行 agent-autoloop status，能看到它接着把活干完。
```

交互终端里直接输入数字回车；非交互终端运行 `agent-autoloop answer 1 2` 选择“绿色”。再跑 `agent-autoloop status`，就能看到它接上刚才的会话并显示“你选了绿色，试跑通过”，还有今天和最近 7 天的轮数、Token 和费用（[统计口径](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#看情况回答)）。

## 一件事怎么转起来

编号和上面的架构图一一对应：

1. **新事件进来。** 早上 9 点的定时任务、GitHub 上新提的 Issue、业务系统报的错，都变成一条标准事件送进内核。
2. **按规则派活。** 内核照你写的规则，决定交给哪个 Agent、去哪个目录干。同一件事排队时又来的消息，会合并成一轮处理。
3. **干完一轮就退出。** Agent 把结果写在最后一条回复里，进程直接退出。
4. **拿不准才问你。** 碰到删数据、重启服务、花钱、对外发消息这类事，内核通过飞书或桌面通知发一张卡片给你。等你回复期间，它不占后台进程，也不消耗 Token。
5. **点一下，接着干。** 你选完，它接上原来的对话，把剩下的活干完。

能自己搞定的事走图上方的自动闭环：直接办完，或者约个时间（比如半小时后）再醒来复查，全程不打扰你。

## 日常怎么配？

### 写一份规则（`rules.json`）

不需要写胶水代码。打开 `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json`，在 `rules` 里写清楚**什么事、交给谁、在哪个目录干**。`to` 填 `agents` 里已有的名字。比如每天早上 9 点写早报：

```json
{
  "name": "早报",
  "when": { "cron": "0 9 * * *" },
  "to": "codex",
  "cwd": "~/notes",
  "prompt": "整理昨天的笔记和提交，写今天的早报。"
}
```

外部事件写法一样，只是要先接好来源。比如有人提新 Issue 时交给 Codex，先按[说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个事件插件)在 `sources` 里登记 `github`：

```json
{
  "name": "处理 issue",
  "when": { "source": "github", "types": ["issues.opened"] },
  "to": "codex",
  "cwd": "~/code/app",
  "skill": "handle-issue",
  "parallel": 3
}
```

`agent-autoloop pause  `、`resume  ` 暂停和恢复一条规则，暂停期间到点不跑、来事件不接，恢复后不补跑；`agent-autoloop run  ` 立即跑一轮。这些记在中台的日志里，不改 `rules.json`。

保存后几秒内自动生效，可以运行 `agent-autoloop check` 检查，`agent-autoloop check  ` 检查一份草稿，不碰正在跑的中台；`agent-autoloop rules explain` 看生效的规则和下次定时，`agent-autoloop emit   --dry-run` 预演一条事件会派给谁（不连接中台、不写日志）。就算改错了，或者文件被删、读不到，系统也会继续按旧规则跑，并发卡片提醒你。

### Agent 怎么跟中台配合？

中台对 Agent 只有一个约定：**在最后一条回复里交代结果**。事情办完了，正常输出一句结论就行。需要向你请示时，在回复末尾附一段 `agent-autoloop` 代码块：

````text
订单已经核对完毕，库存充足。

```agent-autoloop
{
  "ask": [{
    "title": "怎么发货？",
    "text": "两种方式今天都能发出。",
    "options": ["快递", "自提"],
    "key": "shipping"
  }]
}
```
````

除了提问（`ask`），还能发通知（`notice`）、关闭已解决的卡片（`resolve`）、预约复查（`later`）和触发新事件（`events`）。通告不需要回答，但结案时可以顺手写一句处理说明，这句话会留在卡片上；只是告诉一声的通告标成 `fyi`，不带按钮。万一 JSON 写错了，中台只让它在原会话里重写最后这段回复，不会把已经干完的业务重做一遍；重写也失败时，保留原结论并通知你回执没有生效（通用命令没有会话，直接走这一步）。接着旧会话跑也一样：会话接不上才开新的；接上了、干到一半断了，就算没跑成，过几分钟回到原会话重试，不开新会话重做。同一事项的新事件默认开新会话；规则写 `"resume": true` 就接着上一轮的会话。

## 拿来即用的场景模板

每套模板都带规则、任务 Skill 和启用说明。

| 想做什么 | 已经封装好的流程 |
|---|---|
| [每日早报](examples/recipes/morning-brief/README.md) | 默认每天 8 点整理本地笔记和 Git 提交，写入 `briefs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` |
| [跟进 GitHub Issue](examples/recipes/github-issues/README.md) | 每 5 分钟查新 Issue，在本地改代码并通知你查看；不提交、不推送、不回复 Issue |
| [线上告警排查](examples/recipes/ops-alerts/README.md) | 接收报错、对照代码查原因，需要重启时发卡片询问，回答后继续 |
| [用户反馈处理](examples/recipes/feedback/README.md) | 重读反馈当前状态、修复、交付核实、准备回复；需要决定时飞书问你，回答后继续 |
| [网站巡检](examples/recipes/website-watch/README.md) | 每 5 分钟检查状态和关键内容，首次异常交给 Agent，持续异常不重复通知，恢复后更新原卡片 |
| [飞书周报与业务摘要](examples/recipes/feishu-brief/README.md) | 周日 18 点按你的权限读汇报和指定表格，生成本地摘要；飞书只发简短摘要，完整稿留在本机 |
| [收件箱分诊](examples/recipes/inbox-triage/README.md) | 默认每天 8 点读过去 24 小时的未读邮件，写成清单和回复草稿；不发送、不改邮箱状态 |
| [PR 自动交付](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#交付流水线) | 打上 `deliver` 标签后，审查、等 CI、合并、等发布并核对线上版本 |

**启用：** 打开对应说明，把任务 Skill 放进所用 Agent 的 skills 目录，把示例规则合入 `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json`，替换电脑名和路径，再运行 `agent-autoloop check`。

反馈处理、网站巡检、飞书摘要和收件箱分诊默认使用北京时间，只发给本人的飞书私聊。样例数据都是虚构的；脚本和回执只用本地 HTTP 与假飞书 CLI 验证过，没有在真实账号上跑过完整业务。

更多模板：[Claude 委托 Codex 处理网页](examples/recipes/browser-handoff/README.md)、[每周代码清理](examples/skills/weekly-sweep/SKILL.md)、[交付 PR](examples/skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md)。

## 插件体系：四个方向都能自由替换

内置插件随程序安装，填好配置即可启用；第三方插件用 `agent-autoloop add  ` 安装。

| 方向 | 内置 | 配置 |
|---|---|---|
| **事件**：怎么发现新活 | [GitHub Webhook](plugins/github/source.ts)、[GitLab Webhook](plugins/gitlab/source.ts)、[HTTP 接口](docs/protocol.md#来源把世界变成事件)、[定时规则](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#改规则)、[Issue 轮询脚本](examples/watch-github-issues.sh) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个事件插件) |
| **Agent**：谁来干活 | [Claude Code](plugins/claude/agent.ts)、[Codex](plugins/codex/agent.ts)、[ACP](plugins/acp/agent.ts)、[DeepSeek Harness](plugins/dsh/agent.ts)、[通用命令](plugins/command/agent.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个-agent) |
| **通道**：去哪找你拍板 | [桌面通知](plugins/desktop/channel.ts)（默认开启）、[飞书](plugins/feishu/channel.ts)、[钉钉 / 企微 / Slack / Discord](plugins/webhook/templates.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个通道) |
| **交付**：把 CI/CD 也做成插件 | [`delivery`](plugins/delivery/delivery.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#交付流水线) |

**实测情况：** Claude Code、Codex 和 ACP（官方 Codex ACP 适配器）跑通了多轮问答和跨进程会话续接；飞书跑通了发送、按钮回调和卡片更新；四种 Webhook 模板只在本地模拟服务上验证过，GitLab Webhook 按官方文档的格式测试，没连过真实 GitLab。这些文字通道靠回答链接拍板，要把 `hub.publicUrl` 配成手机或电脑能打开的地址。

**内置 Agent 走第三方网关。** Claude Code、Codex 要接第三方模型服务，或者启动前要先设好环境变量，写一个设好变量再启动它的小脚本，在 Agent 里写 `"program": "脚本路径"`，会话续接和用量统计照旧，见[说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个-agent)。

**其他命令行 Agent 一行接入。** 设置 `use: "command"` 并传入命令数组，`{prompt}` 作为独立参数传递，不会被当成 shell 代码执行。下面的命令整理自各家官方文档，我们还没有逐个跑过：

| Agent | 接入命令 |
|---|---|
| [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/cli-help.md#dsh-headless) 旧版（内置插件要 0.2.2 或更新） | `dsh --profile headless {prompt}` |
| [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md) | `pi --print {prompt}` |
| [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/agent) | `openclaw agent exec {prompt}` |
| [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/cli) | `hermes chat -Q -q {prompt}` |
| [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters) | `agent -p --trust {prompt}` |
| [WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.ai/docs/cli/headless) | `codebuddy -p {prompt}` |

会说 ACP 的 Agent 用 `use: "acp"` 接，还能接着原来的会话做：[Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/acp-mode/) 写 `"command": ["gemini", "--acp"]`，[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs/acp) 写 `"command": ["opencode", "acp"]`。这两条已经跑通了 ACP 握手（Gemini CLI 0.67.0、OpenCode 1.1.2），多轮问答和会话续接还没跑过。

**交付流水线。** 给 GitHub PR 打上 `deliver` 标签后，它会自己跟进到上线：**审代码 → 等 CI → 合并 PR → 等部署 → 核对线上版本**。审查和交付配置只从 `main` 读取，绝不在接单电脑上检出或运行 PR 里的代码；排队、并发和重试直接复用内核。

**写自己的插件。** 从 [Agent](examples/plugins/hello-agent/agent.ts)、[通道](examples/plugins/hello-channel/channel.ts)、[事件](examples/plugins/hello-source/source.ts) 三个可运行的最小模板开始，见[插件开发说明](docs/plugins.md)。要让 Agent 操作网页，先看[浏览器接入](docs/plugins.md#浏览器接入)。命令行和 [MCP](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#mcp-与密钥撤销) 也能查看和回答卡片。

## 内核的四个机制

内核约 1850 行代码、零运行时依赖。它不读系统时钟、不用随机数、不向外发请求，插件主动连进来，账号凭据留在各自的插件里；同样的输入永远得出同样的结果。它把四个计算机领域的成熟做法用到了命令行 Agent 上：

- **挂起零消耗**：等你拍板时进程直接退出，等待状态存在数据库里，Agent 不用一直挂着。你三天没回，这三天就没有 Agent 进程在跑、不花 Token，只有很轻的中台在后台等着；你一回答，它接着原来的对话继续干。
- **事件溯源**：所有状态都从一条只追加的日志算出来，日志和索引在同一个事务里写进磁盘，写完才应答。进程被强杀，已经确认的事不丢（整机断电没有单独测过）；任何一轮为什么跑、结果是什么，一条命令就能查清；数据格式变了就从日志重建，不用写迁移脚本。
- **指令数据分离**：思路和 SQL 参数化一样。Issue 的标题和正文等外部文字只作为资料放进文件，不拼进提示词，提示词里只有校验过字符的类型、编号和链接；用哪个 Agent、在哪个目录、什么权限，只由你本机的规则决定，事件里带 `cwd`、`agent`、`access` 字段会被直接拒收。
- **跳数熔断**：思路和网络包的 TTL 一样。Agent 交回的事件会再派给 Agent，层数一路累加，经过人工提问和定时复查也不清零，Agent 自己改不了；超过 8 层就只记录、不再派活，并发一张卡片告诉你。

### 自己跑一遍

Windows 用 `npm run test:windows` 和 `node scripts/install-smoke-windows.ts`，运行共用行为测试与原生进程、安装检查；Unix shell 测试仍在 Linux/macOS 上跑。

在程序目录 `~/.agent-autoloop/app` 下运行：

| 验证什么 | 命令 |
|---|---|
| 任何一轮的来龙去脉 | `agent-autoloop why 1` |
| 20 万步模拟断网、丢包、崩溃和重复提交，一个种子就能复现 | `node sim/random.ts 24301 200000` |
| 强杀进程 1000 次，已确认的记录一条不丢 | `node sim/crash.ts 1000 12648430` |
| 下面的性能数字 | `npm run benchmark` |

```text
第 1 轮 · 演示
11-03 20:47:25  规则版本 #1
11-03 20:47:25  触发事件：来源 local · 类型 demo.start · 对象 example
11-03 20:47:25  local 领取（演示程序）
11-03 20:47:25  结束：演示完成
```

### 实测性能

Apple M5 Pro、24 GB、Node 24.21.0。写入逐条提交，事务落盘后才应答。

| 指标 | 实测 |
|---|---:|
| 冷启动 | 88.78 ms |
| 空闲内存 | 59.94 MB RSS |
| 1000 个同时等待的长轮询 | 170.49 MB RSS |
| 持久化写入 | 2394 条/秒 |
| 派活 p99 | 1.82 ms |
| 排队 5000 时被挡下的心跳 p99 | 1.66 ms |
| 110 万条事实时的启动 | 99.8 ms |
| 内核行数（含空行和注释） | 约 1850 |
| 运行时依赖 | 0 |

历史变大后，状态汇总会变慢，日志和索引也继续占磁盘；格式变化后的首次启动要从日志全量重建，110 万条用时 43.1 秒。[完整数据和测法](docs/protocol.md#历史增长实测)。

## 用量与合规说明

中台直接调用你本机已经安装并登录好的命令行工具，不会读取或转存你的账号凭据。模型调用消耗算在你自己的账号名下，额度和使用范围遵循各家模型厂商的服务条款。

在高频自动化场景下，各家厂商通常更建议使用 API Key（个人订阅额度主要是为日常人工交互设计的，详见 [Anthropic](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) 与 [OpenAI](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth) 的官方说明）。如果你用它对外提供服务，请使用 API Key。本项目为独立开源项目，与上述厂商无隶属或背书关系。

## 更多文档

- [安装说明](INSTALL.md)
- [规则与交付流水线配置手册](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md)
- [如何编写插件](docs/plugins.md)
- [完整通信协议](docs/protocol.md)
- [安全边界说明](SECURITY.md)
- [参与贡献与交流](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [项目开发约定](AGENTS.md)

  仓库目录

| 位置 | 放什么 |
|---|---|
| `kernel/` | 内核：决策、事实日志、状态投影、到期任务、规则匹配、接口行为与卡片表单 |
| `host/` | 运行外壳：Node HTTP、文件与 SQLite 连接、时钟、配置、状态汇总、后台服务和插件加载 |
| `protocol/` | 通信格式、JSON Schema、输入校验、HTTP 客户端和一致性检查 |
| `worker/` | 接单程序：领活、运行 Agent、心跳与停止、读取和提交回执 |
| `cli/`、`bin/` | 用户命令及启动入口，包括状态、回答、`why`、MCP、更新与卸载 |
| `plugins/` | 内置 Agent、事件、通道和交付插件 |
| `examples/recipes/` | 完整场景：规则、任务 Skill 和启用说明 |
| `examples/plugins/`、`examples/skills/`、`examples/*.sh` | 最小插件模板、独立任务手册和 Shell 示例 |
| `skills/agent-autoloop/` | 中台的正式配置与操作手册，安装时也提供给 Agent 使用 |
| `docs/` | 通信协议、插件开发说明与中英文架构图 |
| `tests/`、`sim/` | 日常行为测试，以及模拟、穷举、强杀和变异检查 |
| `scripts/`、`.github/workflows/` | 性能与真机验证、安装冒烟脚本，以及 Windows / Linux / macOS CI |
| 根目录文档与 `install.sh` | 中英文 README、安装说明、安全边界、开发约定、许可证与安装脚本 |

读代码可以从 `bin/agent-autoloop.ts` → `cli/main.ts` 开始，再按功能进入 `host/`、`worker/` 或 `plugins/`；内核设计先看[协议](docs/protocol.md)。同名文件分属不同层：`host/http.ts` 转换 Node 请求，`kernel/http.ts` 定义接口行为；`protocol/rules.ts` 校验输入，`kernel/rules.ts` 定义规则类型和匹配。

**[下载 Windows 版](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai/releases/latest)** · [使用指南](docs/USAGE.md) · [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md) · [反馈问题](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai/issues)

岛仔是一款开源的 Windows 桌面小工具。平时收起在屏幕边缘，鼠标靠近就展开；切歌、看日程、复制验证码、记一条待办，都能顺手完成。小岛里的伙伴会眨眼、打盹、喝水，也会跟着音乐唱歌。

你可以选刘海或胶囊，放在顶部、左侧或右侧，只保留自己需要的功能。岛仔使用 Rust 和 egui 构建，不依赖 Electron。

## 微信里有新消息，看一眼岛边

微信和 QQ 未读：收起时显示图标，展开后点击切换对应窗口

- **微信、QQ 未读提醒**：收起时亮起图标和红点，展开后在面板旁查看，点击切换到对应窗口。
- **微信多开分开看**：不同账号分别显示，点击对应账号的未读图标即可切换。
- **按需显示通知正文**：默认隐藏正文；开启预览后仍遮罩识别出的验证码。
- **微信提醒不读取聊天正文**：根据任务栏闪动提示新消息。微信缩在托盘时，可选开启「托盘一键唤起微信」。

开启方式：**设置 → 通知、邮箱与日程 → 通知**。微信开启「微信新消息提醒」；QQ 选择「只连接 QQ」，并在 QQ 中启用 Windows 系统通知。

## 换个皮肤，也换个位置

五款皮肤：经典黑、奶油、毛玻璃浅色、毛玻璃深色、悬浮云；刘海和胶囊两种形态

**五款皮肤 × 两种形态，自由搭配。** 经典黑、奶油、毛玻璃·浅、毛玻璃·深和「悬浮云」，都能搭配刘海或胶囊。毛玻璃透出身后的桌面；悬浮云随专辑封面换色，光晕跟着鼠标移动。

顶部、左侧和右侧停靠，以及侧边收起与展开状态

- **三边停靠**：顶部横向展开，左右侧边收起为竖向胶囊，靠近后从屏幕边缘展开。
- **大小与位置可调**：岛体大小支持 80%–140%；顶部可左右移动，侧边可上下调整。
- **多屏与自动避让**：跟随主屏或固定到指定显示器；指定应用覆盖小岛时，可自动收成贴边细线。
- **按习惯显示**：支持极简模式、12／24 小时制，以及功能页面开关与拖动排序。

在 **设置 → 常规 → 岛体外观／岛体显示** 中调整。岛上单行歌词目前支持顶部停靠。

## 听歌时，歌词就在抬眼处

音乐播放控制、展开歌词与收起状态下的岛上单行歌词

播放、暂停、切歌、调节音量和拖动进度，都能在岛上操作。展开看歌词，也可以收起后只留一行歌词，让桌面继续做自己的事。

- 通过 Windows 媒体会话读取播放信息，并针对网易云音乐、QQ 音乐、酷狗、汽水音乐补充兼容。
- 网易云优先按歌曲 ID 找词，改善译名、合唱署名和 Live／Remix 等不同版本的匹配。

播放器需提供可用的媒体信息；歌词取决于歌曲元数据与歌词来源，个别歌曲或播放器版本可能无法显示。

## 日程、待办和专注，放在一起

日历与会议安排、每周重复待办、番茄专注与饮水提醒

| 想做的事 | 岛仔能帮你 |
| --- | --- |
| 看今天的安排 | 月历与当日时间线，合并多个日历和正式邮件邀请，提前提醒会议 |
| 记住每周的事 | 待办支持单次提醒、每周指定日期重复或每天重复；下一次到来时恢复为待办 |
| 专心做一件事 | 专注与休息计时，收起时也能查看进度 |
| 记得喝水 | 自定义每日目标、单次饮水量、提醒间隔与时段，记录错误可撤销 |

日历可接入 **飞书、钉钉、企业微信、iCloud、自定义 CalDAV 和兼容的 Exchange ActiveSync**，也能导入 `.ics` 文件。相同日程合并去重；支持全天、跨天和重复日程。

本机新建或导入的日程保存在本机；远程日历为只读同步。程序退出、电脑关机或睡眠期间无法持续提醒。

## 文件先放岛上，刚复制的字也能找回

文件置物架与剪贴板历史：拖入文件、重新复制文字、固定常用内容

**文件置物架**：拖入文件临时收集，点击打开、定位原文件，或拖出到其他应用。移除记录不会删除原文件。

**文字剪贴板**：找回最近复制的 30 条文字，点一下重新复制，常用内容可以固定。历史保存在本机，重启后仍可查看；可在 **设置 → 待办与置物 → 剪贴板** 中关闭。密码管理器标记为敏感的内容不记录。

## 验证码少切一次窗口，邮件也能直接读

验证码大卡点击复制与邮件正文阅读

连接多个邮箱，在岛上查看来信、识别验证码并点击复制。邮件支持正文阅读与独立全文窗口，网页链接交给默认浏览器打开；正式日历邀请可进入日程。支持已读／未读切换、全部已读、移到回收站及恢复；默认仅在本机整理，可在邮件设置中开启「同步邮件操作到邮箱」。

支持 **QQ、163、126、腾讯企业邮、iCloud、Gmail 和自定义 IMAP**。验证码可设置在 30／60／300 秒后自动隐藏，覆盖列表、正文与通知；主动查看后会再次隐藏。

## AI 还剩多少额度，抬眼就知道

AI 额度面板：Codex 额度、WorkBuddy 积分与 DeepSeek 余额

支持 **Codex、Claude、Kimi、Grok Bot、Gemini、ZCode、WorkBuddy 和 DeepSeek**。

订阅额度、重置时间、套餐积分与 API 余额，按服务展示。多个账号可分别命名、选择配色，常用账号直接放在收起的小岛上。

- **ZCode**：查看套餐额度。
- **Claude**：只读取桌面版本地用量历史与缓存，或接收 Claude Code 官方状态栏输出；岛仔不使用 Claude 登录令牌，也不请求 Claude 额度接口。数据随官方客户端使用更新，桌面版缓存有效时自动显示重置时间，读取不到时显示未知。
- **WorkBuddy**：查看剩余积分；优先识别本机客户端登录，也可在默认浏览器完成授权。
- **DeepSeek**：使用 API Key 连接，查看账户余额、充值与赠送金额。

连接方式、可用字段与账号订阅有关；请求失败或登录过期时，以对应服务的官方页面为准。

## 还有这些顺手的小功能

电源与电量、网络变化、音量、大写锁定、输入语言、蓝牙设备状态，都能在小岛上提示。通知、蓝牙监听与不常用的功能页可以按需关闭。

## 下载安装

前往 **[最新正式版](https://github.com/Renly1994/xiaotang-daozai/releases/latest)**，按使用习惯选择：

| 下载文件 | 使用方式 |
| --- | --- |
| `Daozai-Setup-v版本号-x64.exe` | **推荐**。双击安装，可选择安装位置、桌面快捷方式和开机自启 |
| `Daozai-v版本号-windows-x64.zip` | 免安装。完整解压后运行 `daozai.exe`，用户数据仍保存在应用数据目录 |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | 下载校验，可用 PowerShell `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` 比对 |

首次安装默认创建桌面快捷方式、不开机自启。安装后从小岛或托盘打开设置，选择需要的功能和连接。

**更新**：设置 → 关于 → 检查更新。支持应用内下载、校验后重启更新，也可从发布页下载覆盖安装；升级保留原设置和数据，卸载同样保留用户数据。下载窗口提供夸克网盘备用入口。

**系统**：Windows 10／11 x64。默认使用 OpenGL，初始化失败时自动尝试 Direct3D 12。Windows 11 已进行本机实测，Windows 10、不同显卡及多屏组合仍需更多反馈。暂不提供 macOS、Linux 或 ARM64 成品包。

当前程序未做商业代码签名，Windows 可能提示未知发布者；请核对仓库来源与文件校验值。更多操作见 [使用指南](docs/USAGE.md)。

  连接服务之前，需要准备什么？

| 类型 | 支持入口 | 需要准备 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 邮箱 | QQ、163、126、腾讯企业邮、iCloud、Gmail、自定义 IMAP | 启用 IMAP，填写授权码或 App 专用密码；自定义服务可填写服务器、端口与登录用户名 |
| 日历 | 飞书、钉钉、企业微信、iCloud、CalDAV、Exchange ActiveSync | 服务商提供的日历同步凭据与必要的服务器地址；安装桌面客户端不等于授权 |
| AI 额度 | Codex、Claude、Kimi、Grok Bot、Gemini、ZCode、WorkBuddy、DeepSeek | 对应客户端登录、独立授权或 API Key；具体以设置中的连接入口为准 |

QQ 收信、邮件日程和飞书个人日历已进行真实账号测试。其他日历入口的可用性与服务端配置、权限和兼容性有关；钉钉、企业微信尚未完成本轮真实账号同步验收。

  数据与隐私

- 设置、待办、本机日程、饮水记录、剪贴板历史、置物路径与连接元数据保存在 `%APPDATA%\Daozai`。
- 邮箱和日历密码、DeepSeek API Key 保存在 Windows 凭据管理器；独立 Gemini、WorkBuddy 会话使用 Windows DPAPI 加密。
- 微信新消息提醒根据任务栏闪动工作，不读取联系人或聊天正文；QQ 与应用通知需要相应的系统通知权限。
- 读取已有 AI 客户端登录时不回写原客户端配置。不要把授权码、Cookie、API Key 或登录 JSON 上传到 Issue。
- 邮箱读取收件箱，不读取垃圾邮件文件夹；邮件正文在当前进程中用于展示和识别。
- 岛仔没有自建的邮件或日程上传后台；开启联网功能后，会访问对应服务商与歌词服务。

完整说明见 [隐私与安全](docs/PRIVACY.md)。

  从源码构建与参与开发

需要 Rust stable、MSVC C++ 构建工具和 Windows SDK。

```powershell
rustup default stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
cargo build --locked --release --bin daozai
.\target\release\daozai.exe
```

运行测试及打包：

```powershell
cargo test --locked --all-targets --features record -- --test-threads=1
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\package.ps1
```

测试按单线程运行，以隔离使用进程环境变量的数据目录测试。低内存设备可设置 `$env:CARGO_BUILD_JOBS = "1"`。打包需要 NSIS 3，可通过 `-NsisCompiler` 指定 `makensis.exe`。

项目结构、界面预览与贡献方式见 [开发指南](CONTRIBUTING.md)。

## 开源与致谢

岛仔原创代码采用 [MIT License](LICENSE)。Rust 依赖、vendored 代码、第三方图标及品牌标识沿用各自的许可或权利声明；MIT 不授予服务商标使用权，也不代表官方合作或认证。详见 [第三方声明](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt) 和 [依赖说明](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md)。

「悬浮云」皮肤作者：啵（[@hanhb123](https://github.com/hanhb123)）。感谢 egui／eframe、Rust 社区，以及提供参考与素材的开源项目。

## 感谢支持

感谢支持岛仔的朋友们

喜欢岛仔的话，欢迎点一个 **Star**，也可以在 **设置 → 关于 → 支持作者** 请岛仔喝杯咖啡。

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# One VM for every project

An isolated sandbox with your project's toolchain, ready for you or a coding agent to start coding.

[Install](https://devvm.dev/docs/getting-started/install/) · [Read the docs](https://devvm.dev/docs/) · [Staying safe](https://devvm.dev/docs/safety/)

## Install

On macOS, install devvm with Homebrew, which also installs Lima:

```sh
brew trust --formula devvmhq/tap/devvm
brew install devvmhq/tap/devvm
```

On Linux, install it with the install script, which also works on macOS and asks before it installs Lima, QEMU or access to `/dev/kvm`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/devvmhq/devvm/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

Then run `devvm doctor`, which checks what devvm needs on your machine and says how to get anything that's missing.

Each release is signed with devvm's minisign key, `RWSjzFsn7ETaijKJ2y7F4DtZobXmyv+LmdclJwZP/KmAkLUwOCzWF/2b`, and [Checking the install script](https://devvm.dev/docs/internals/install/#checking-the-install-script) shows how to check the script with it before you run it.

- **Requirements:** macOS 13 or newer, or Linux, on arm64 or x86_64, with Lima 2.2 or newer ([Lima's requirements](https://devvm.dev/docs/backends/lima/#requirements)).
- **Tested on** Apple silicon Macs and on Linux on arm64 and x86_64, but not yet on Intel Macs.
- [Installing](https://devvm.dev/docs/getting-started/install/) has the full list of requirements and the install script's options, and [Upgrading and uninstalling](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/upgrading/) covers what comes later.

## Quick start

```sh
cd ~/some-project
devvm
```

1. **Go to your project.** Open a terminal and `cd` into any project folder.
2. **Run devvm.** It shows what this folder's new VM gets, with the toolchains your project's files call for. Confirm to make the VM, or customize it to choose its toolchains, coding agents, layers, network tier and size.
3. **Start your agent.** devvm opens a shell in the VM, at the same path as on your machine, and its prompt starts with `(devvm)`, so run `claude` there.

- Running `devvm` in the folder again opens the same VM.
- [Your first VM](https://devvm.dev/docs/getting-started/first-vm/) has the rest.

> [!NOTE]
> The first run starts with a few questions that set devvm's defaults for every new VM and its base image: the size and coding agents new VMs get, and the base image's optional extras. It builds the base image once, in a few minutes. Later VMs start in seconds.

> [!TIP]
> Claude Code needs your Claude login before its first start, which `devvm agent login claude` makes from the VM and keeps on your machine ([Claude Code's login](https://devvm.dev/docs/getting-started/first-vm/#claude-codes-login)).

## What's supported

- **Toolchains:** devvm detects them from the project's files, so a folder with `package.json` gets node, and the [toolchains](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/toolchains/) page lists them all.
- **Coding agents:** Claude Code, Codex, opencode and pi run in the VM, with your settings, skills and MCP servers. devvm keeps their settings and logins in a store of its own, and `devvm agent import` copies them in from an agent you already use on your machine ([coding agents](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/coding-agents/)).
- **Layers:** the built-in `docker`, `nix` and `desktop` layers, and your own from `devvm layer new` ([layers](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/images/#layers)).
- **Backend:** devvm runs its VMs on [Lima](https://lima-vm.io) ([backends](https://devvm.dev/docs/backends/)).

## Why use devvm?

- **Isolated:** each project folder gets a VM of its own, which mounts only the project folder, at the same path as on your machine ([what a VM can reach](https://devvm.dev/docs/safety/#what-a-vm-can-reach)).
- **Network tiers:** new VMs get the allowlist tier by default, so they reach only the hosts you allow ([network tiers](https://devvm.dev/docs/safety/network/)).
- **Secrets stay home:** on every tier, your secrets, such as your GitHub token and Claude Code token, stay on your machine.
- **Agents in the sandbox:** you start the agent in the VM's shell, so you never install it on your machine.
- **Ready in seconds:** every VM is a copy of a base image, and toolchains are shared read-only between VMs ([images](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/images/)).
- **No sandbox closes every gap:** a few habits close most of what devvm can't close on its own, so read [Staying safe](https://devvm.dev/docs/safety/) before you trust a VM with a project.

## Working on a clone

By default, the VM mounts your project folder, so the VM and your editor share the same files. With `devvm --clone`, the VM gets a clone of the repo of its own, so nothing in it can touch your working tree or `.git`, and its work reaches your repo only when you fetch it:

```sh
devvm --clone                 # make the VM with its own clone, and open a shell in it
git fetch devvm               # later, on this machine, fetch the VM's work as devvm/
git log -p main..devvm/main   # review it before you merge it
```

[Working on a clone](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/clone/) has the details.

## Docs

The docs are at [devvm.dev](https://devvm.dev/), and their source is in `docs/`.

- [Getting started](https://devvm.dev/docs/getting-started/): installing devvm, your first VM and the commands you use most.
- [Using devvm](https://devvm.dev/docs/using/): images and tools, clones, links between VMs, ports and size, coding agents, SSH and editors, and troubleshooting.
- [Staying safe](https://devvm.dev/docs/safety/): the habits that keep you safe, network tiers, `.git` protection and attack vectors.
- [Backends](https://devvm.dev/docs/backends/): Lima, which runs the VMs, and what it gives them.
- [Compared to other tools](https://devvm.dev/docs/compared/): how devvm differs from Docker Sandboxes and other sandboxes.
- [CLI reference](https://devvm.dev/docs/cli/): every command, with its arguments and flags.
- [How it works](https://devvm.dev/docs/internals/): how devvm does what it does, for checking a claim or reviewing its security.
- [Contributing](https://devvm.dev/docs/contributing/): building, testing and writing docs.

## Security and contributing

- Report a vulnerability as [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) says.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [Contributing](https://devvm.dev/docs/contributing/) pages cover building, testing and writing docs.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# HomeRoll

**A native iOS photos app for your own [Immich](https://immich.app) server – the look and feel of the iPhone Photos app, without iCloud.**

HomeRoll is an independent iPhone client for a self-hosted Immich server. It aims to feel like Apple's Photos app on iOS 26 (grid, zoom levels, viewer, editor, memories, search, people …) while all photos stay on hardware you own.

> **Status:** works and is used daily against Immich v3.3.5 with ~85,000 photos and videos. UI in **English and German** (follows the iPhone language; more translations welcome). Code comments are in German.
>
> Built with help from [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code): I did the research (Apple's Photos frameworks analysed with [rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea)), the design decisions and daily testing on my own iPhone, a lot of the Swift was written together with it.
>
> **Personal project:** I use it every day and keep it working as long as I need it myself. No guarantees, no support promises. Bug reports and pull requests are welcome, but I answer when I have time.
>
> Not affiliated with Apple or with Immich/FUTO. "Immich" is a trademark of its owners.
>
> **On a Mac?** [HomeRoll Desktop](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeRoll-Desk) is the macOS sibling – edits made there look the same on the iPhone.

  Screenshots with public-domain sample photos (NASA/Kennedy Space Center, ISS crew).

## Features

**Library**
- Albums, Favorites, Trips and People with the same pinch-to-zoom grid and *Newest/Oldest first* sorting
- Timeline for 80,000+ items, smooth scrolling (UIKit grid, ThumbHash placeholders, month-wise loading, newest first)
- Zoom levels like Photos: 1 / 3 / 5 columns, months, years – pinch to zoom
- Swipe-to-select with auto-scroll, context menus, drag & drop into other apps
- Videos, Live Photos and slo-mos play muted in the 1-column view
- Fully offline: the timeline and all previews are stored on the device

**Viewer**
- Full-resolution original when zooming, HDR (gain map) on device
- Live Photos: short motion when swiping to them, press to play; loop, bounce, long exposure
- Video bar with filmstrip, scrubbing, sound, AirPlay; HDR video originals
- Slo-mo: 120/240 fps videos play slowed down in the middle, like Photos
- **Spatial scene** (photos with depth data): tilt the iPhone for a 3D effect (subject via Vision, depth layers, pivot on the subject, background filled by the server)
- Info: people (name them right there), albums, source app ("Saved from WhatsApp"), camera, map, caption
- Live Text and Visual Look Up (animals, plants, landmarks)
- Comments and likes in shared albums

**Editing**
- 15 adjustment sliders + Auto in Photos' order, Photographic Styles, filters with strength, crop/straighten with auto
- Portrait: change the aperture afterwards (own depth blur)
- Clean Up: wipe away objects (LaMa on your server)
- Markup (PencilKit), video trim (lossless) and mute, slo-mo range, Live Photo key frame
- Edits are saved as a new version, stacked with the original on the server

**Search, people, collections**
- Live search with combinable chips (person, place, country, album, media type, year), text in images, smart search with a relevance check
- Siri / Shortcuts action "Fotos suchen"
- People & pets: name, favorite, merge, hide, birthday, "Is this X?" suggestions
- Albums, media types (videos, selfies, Live, portrait, panorama, time-lapse, slo-mo, bursts, screenshots, receipts, handwriting, QR codes, duplicates, **large videos**), map with photo stacks
- Hidden and Recently Deleted locked with Face ID

**Memories**
- On this day, trips, best of the year, seasons, places over the years, **birthdays**
- Player with scenes in rhythm, music moods, "Up next", export as video, create your own
- Sensitive photos (wounds, IDs, letters, screenshots, receipts) are kept out of memories and featured photos

**Backup & system**
- Backup engine: new iPhone photos and videos as originals (checksum dedupe, Live Photos, favorites, hidden, edited stacks, local time)
- Backs up the entire library by default (iCloud-only photos are downloaded for it); already imported older photos another way, e.g. with icloudpd? Set the date and only newer ones are backed up
- **Free Up Space**: delete from the iPhone only what is verified on your server (backup checksum + server check, not in the server trash), by age, favorites kept; iOS asks first and keeps them 30 days in Recently Deleted
- Widgets (Memories, Featured Photos), share extension ("save to my server" from any app)
- Shared links, Immich partner sharing ("shared library")
- Per-account separation of caches and memories, performance log

## Requirements

- An Immich server (tested with **v3.3.5**) reachable from the iPhone – at home or via VPN (e.g. WireGuard)
- Xcode 26, [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) (`brew install xcodegen`)
- iPhone with iOS 26

Optional server add-ons (see [`server/README.md`](server/README.md)): relevance service (better smart search, face suggestions, sensitive-photo check), categories service (receipts, documents …) and Clean Up (LaMa). The app works without them – those features are then simply hidden or less precise.

## Install without a Mac

You need your own Immich server for this. **Step-by-step guide from zero (server, access from outside, install, backup): [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md).**

1. Download `HomeRoll- .ipa` (e.g. `HomeRoll-1.0.3.ipa`) from the [latest release](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeRoll/releases/latest).
2. Install it with [SideStore](https://sidestore.io) or [AltStore](https://altstore.io). A free Apple ID is enough, the app then has to be refreshed every 7 days (SideStore does that on the phone).
3. Open the app and log in with your Immich server address and your Immich account.

### Verify the download

Every release lists the file's SHA-256 (GitHub also shows it as the asset "digest"). Check it before installing:

```bash
shasum -a 256 HomeRoll- .ipa
```

## Build & install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ /homeroll.git
cd homeroll
xcodegen generate
open HomeRoll.xcodeproj
```

1. Set your own **bundle identifier prefix** and **App Group** in `project.yml` (defaults: `org.homeroll.app`, `group.org.homeroll.app`) and select your team in Xcode.
2. Run on your iPhone. Log in with your Immich server address (e.g. `https://photos.example.com` or `http://192.168.x.y:2283`) and your Immich account.
3. Unsigned IPA for sideloading (AltStore/SideStore): `./build-ipa.sh`.

If your server uses a certificate from your own home CA, put the CA certificate as `Resources/HeimnetzCA.der` into the project and add it to the `HomeRoll` target sources in `project.yml` – the app will then trust it in addition to the system CAs.

### Simulator with a test account

```bash
echo " " > ~/.homeroll-token   # never commit this
FOTOS_SERVER=http:// :2283 FOTOS_TOKEN_FILE=~/.homeroll-token ./sim-run.sh
```

Debug builds also read `FOTOS_BACKUP_OFF=1` (no backup), `FOTOS_DUMP_MEMORIES=1` and `FOTOS_DUMP_SPATIAL=1` (debug output in the app's `tmp/`).

## Privacy

- The app talks **only** to your Immich server (and Apple Maps for place search, Apple's on-device Vision for Live Text, Look Up and subject masks).
- No analytics, no third-party SDKs.
- Login token in the Keychain; the share extension and widgets get it via the App Group.

## Project layout

```
App/          SwiftUI/UIKit app (API, Library, Viewer, Editor, Collections, Search, Backup, Core)
Widget/       WidgetKit extension
Share/        Share extension
Shared/       code shared between app and extensions
server/       optional add-on services next to Immich (Docker)
tools/        icon generator
```

## License

[GPL-3.0](LICENSE) (GNU General Public License v3.0; releases up to this change were published under MIT). Third-party: Immich (AGPL-3.0) is not included – HomeRoll only talks to its HTTP API. The Clean Up service downloads the LaMa model (Apache-2.0) at build time.

---

## More Home apps

Same idea, other Apple apps – all free, open source and self-hosted:

- **[HomeRoll Desktop](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeRoll-Desk)** – Photos for Mac · Immich
- **[HomeRoll TV](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeRoll-TV)** – Photos for Apple TV · Immich
- **[HomeTune](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeTune)** – Music · Navidrome
- **[HomeNotes](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeNotes)** – Notes · Nextcloud
- **[HomePost](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomePost)** – Mail · IMAP/SMTP or JMAP
- **[HomeFind](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeFind)** – Find My · Dawarich
- **[HomeCast](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeCast)** – Podcasts · PinePods
- **[HomeThread](https://github.com/silentprovider423/HomeThread)** – notes to self · own server (Docker)

All apps: [github.com/silentprovider423](https://github.com/silentprovider423)

## Deutsch

**HomeRoll** ist eine eigene iPhone-Fotos-App für deinen selbst betriebenen Immich-Server. Sie sieht aus und fühlt sich an wie Apples Fotos-App unter iOS 26, aber alle Fotos bleiben auf deiner eigenen Hardware, ohne iCloud. Die Oberfläche gibt es auf Deutsch und Englisch, je nach Sprache des iPhones. Funktionen, Voraussetzungen und Installation stehen oben.

## Advantages of the platform

### Multitenant ecosystem
* A set of interrelated subsystems: MapReduce, an SQL query engine, a job schedule, and a key-value store for OLTP workloads.
* Support for large numbers of users that eliminates multiple installations and streamlines hardware usage
### Reliability and stability
* No single point of failure
* Automated replication between servers
* Updates with no loss of computing progress
### Scalability
* Up to 1 million CPU cores and thousands of GPUs
* Exabytes of data on different media: HDD, SSD, NVME, RAM
* Tens of thousands of nodes
* Automated server up and down-scaling
### Rich functionality
* Expansive MapReduce module
* Distributed ACID transactions
* A variety of SDKs and APIs
* Secure isolation for compute resources and storage
* User-friendly and easy-to-use UI
### YTsaurus Flow
* Native framework for real-time data stream processing
* Efficient stateful computations for recommendation and content systems
* Complex pipeline topologies with automatic partitioning and balancing
* Exactly-once processing by default
### CHYT powered by ClickHouse®
* A well-known SQL dialect and familiar functionality
* Fast analytic queries
* Integration with popular BI solutions via JDBC and ODBC
### SPYT powered by Apache Spark
* A set of popular tools for writing ETL processes
* Launch and support for multiple mini SPYT clusters
* Easy migration for ready-made solutions

# Isoform

A proactive personal AI. Works ahead. Lives on your computer.

[Download for Mac](https://www.isoform.ai/download/mac) · [iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/isoform/id6827347350) · [Reserve your name for Agent of You](https://www.isoform.ai/agents)

## What it does

- **Briefs before you ask.** Morning and evening briefs bring together what moved, what's next, and what needs your attention. Find them on Today, in the menu bar, and on a paired iPhone.
- **Needs you.** Review drafts and decisions waiting for you. A proposed reply waits for you to send it.
- **Chat with context.** Ask about your work and Isoform can bring relevant memories and know-how into the conversation.
- **How you do things.** Isoform learns reusable know-how from your work, with the moments and sources it learned from.
- **About you.** A portrait brings together what Isoform has learned about your work, preferences, and interests. You can review and correct it.
- **Tasks.** Give Isoform work to do with your signed-in Claude Code or Codex and see what is running, done, or waiting for you.

**Agent of You: reservations open.** Once Isoform knows how you work, other people can hire an agent that works like you, on your computer, and you're paid by the minute. Today it's a name reservation, not a live marketplace. [Reserve your name](https://www.isoform.ai/agents).

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Observe on this computer] --> B[Memory on disk]
    B --> C[Your AI: Claude Code, Codex or Ollama]
    C --> D[Briefs, drafts and tasks]
    D  |End-to-end encrypted| E[Paired phone]
```

Memory on disk gives you a record on your computer that you can review and control. Isoform builds on AI tools you already use instead of shipping its own model. Claude Code, Codex, or Ollama handles the model work while Isoform brings in context from your day.

## Privacy

Screenshots, audio recordings, and memory are stored on this computer. Proposed messages and posts to other people wait for your approval; the table shows what can leave your computer as part of using Isoform.

| What leaves | Where and when | How to turn it off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text needed for a task | Your selected AI when Isoform prepares a brief or runs a task. | Pause observing, stop the task, or use a local model for requests. |
| Cropped WeChat screenshots | Your selected AI when Isoform processes observed WeChat activity. | Turn off **Watch my screen** or exclude WeChat from observing. |
| Briefs, including spoken briefs | Your paired phone through an end-to-end encrypted relay, when phone delivery is enabled. | Disconnect the phone or turn off its connection in Settings. |
| Diagnostic events | PostHog when diagnostic sharing is enabled. | Turn off **Share diagnostic data** in Settings > Privacy. |
| Topic names and short search phrases | A web search provider when **Find new things on my topics** is enabled or you request a search. | Turn off **Find new things on my topics** and avoid requesting searches. |

Isoform filters detected sensitive information, including passwords, codes, and card numbers, from observed content. Detection is best effort; see [PII handling](wails-gui/internal/pii/README.md).

## Try it in 60 seconds

1. [Download Isoform for Mac](https://www.isoform.ai/download/mac). It requires macOS 14 or later and supports Apple silicon and Intel.
2. Open the app and follow setup.

## Build from source

Install Go 1.25 or later, Node.js 20.19 or later, pnpm, and the [Wails v2 CLI](https://wails.io/docs/gettingstarted/installation). The build uses bundled dependencies; the `download-*.sh` scripts in `wails-gui/scripts/` prepare them when needed. See [development](docs/development.md) for details.

```bash
./wails-gui/scripts/start-wails-gui.sh
./wails-gui/scripts/build-wails.sh
```

The first command starts the development app; the second creates a production build.

## Releases

See the [release pipeline](docs/release/pipeline.md) for release checks and publication. Local notarization uses a working `APPLE_NOTARY_KEYCHAIN_PROFILE` (default `isoform-notary`), then an App Store Connect API key, then Apple ID credentials. Set `APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_PATH`, `APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_ID`, and `APPLE_NOTARY_ISSUER` to override the API key; the ID and issuer default to `ISOFORM_ASC_KEY_ID` and `ISOFORM_ASC_ISSUER_ID` or the Isoform iPhone upload values, and the path defaults to `~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_ .p8`. The key file remains in place. The release preflight checks the selected credentials with Apple before building.

## FAQ

**Do I need an API key?** No. Isoform can use your signed-in Claude Code or Codex account. An API key is optional.

**Does it work offline or with a local model?** Isoform can use a local Ollama model as a fallback. Cloud models and the phone relay need a network connection; full offline behavior depends on the features and models you use.

**What does it cost?** Isoform uses your existing AI subscriptions and does not require a new Isoform model subscription. Your AI provider's plan and usage limits apply.

**What about Windows, Linux, and iPhone?** The desktop download is for macOS. Windows and Linux are planned; the [iPhone companion is available on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/isoform/id6827347350) and pairs with the desktop app.

## Roadmap

- Windows and Linux
- Agent of You
- Teams

The iPhone app is already on the App Store.

## Repository and contributing

The desktop app is in `wails-gui/`, the agent runtime is in `yansu-agent/`, and the phone and relay live in `ios/`, `relay/`, and `mobile-protocol/`. See [development](docs/development.md) for setup and tests. Open an issue or pull request describing the change and how you tested it.

## Credits

Built on [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code), [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/), [magpie](https://github.com/yetone/magpie), [Wails](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails), and [dumbpipe](https://github.com/n0-computer/dumbpipe) / [iroh](https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh).

## License

Isoform is open source under the [Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-ALv2)](LICENSE.md); each version becomes Apache 2.0 two years after release.

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# qwenFS: Qwen keeps its own files

**qwenFS is an experimental model: Qwen3.5-2B with a filesystem compiled and inserted directly
into its weights.** It is not a plugin, a tool server or a database behind an API. The
filesystem is 8 transformer layers in front of Qwen's own 24, and none of their weights are
learned: every one is set by construction. Qwen saves, reads, organizes and links its own files
through its normal tool calls, and the model answers every call itself.

qwenFS saving a file and reading it back: the FS layers, the file table and the copy layer, token by token

## How it works

**The calls.** Qwen writes ordinary Qwen3.5 tool calls. The circuit reads each call as Qwen
writes it, keying on the single tokens Qwen's tool-call format always uses (`=name`, `=text`,
`=target`, `>`, newline, ` `, …). A call's kind comes from its parameters; only
`unlink_files` is told apart by its function-name token. After ` `, the circuit
prints the tool response itself, in a user turn as Qwen's chat template has it, then opens a new
assistant turn, and Qwen answers.

| Tool | What it does | The circuit's response |
|---|---|---|
| `write_file(name, text)` | save a file (replaces it) | `saved` and the path |
| `append_file(name, text)` | add text to a file, on a new line | `saved` and the path |
| `read_file(name)` | read a file, token for token | the stored text, or `not found` |
| `list_files()` | every file | one path per line, or `empty` |
| `link_files(name, target)` | link a file to another | `linked` and both paths |
| `unlink_files(name, target)` | remove that link | `removed` and both paths |
| `list_links(file)` | files a file links to | one path per line, or `empty` |
| `list_backlinks(path)` | files that link to a file | one path per line, or `empty` |
| `search_files(query)` | files whose text has a word | one path per line, or `empty` |

Paths make folders (`people/alice.txt`, `projects/cafe.txt`); links and backlinks make a graph.

**Where the filesystem lives.** Every part of the model has a job:

- **Attention** holds the files. A write's text stays in the copy layer's attention log, keyed by
  (file index, version, offset); a read is an exact copy, token by token. Each write or append
  is a segment, a version of its own: a file is its segments since its last write, and a read
  copies them in order, printing the next segment's read ack at the end of each one. The ack
  restarts the offset count, so a file can be far longer than one write. A second attention
  layer looks paths up: a path finds its file's index, or falls back to "not found". A third,
  the seek layer, holds a row per word and per link. Every word of a written text is a row,
  keyed by (file index, base, the word's tokens); a search checks one file per response token
  against that file's current base, so a word only an old version had is not found. A link or
  unlink that changes a pair adds a row, +1 or -1; one that changes nothing prints a no-op
  variant of "linked" / "removed" and adds none, so a pair's rows alternate and it is linked
  when they average above 0. A link listing checks one file per token the same way.
- **Gated DeltaNet state** holds the tables and registers: the version, base and path tables
  (128 rows each, one per file, which is what sets the file limit), the file count and the
  call's state.
- **MLPs** parse the tool calls and pick every forced token: acks, the response frame, echoed
  paths, each file's marker or skip in a search or link listing. A file a listing passes over
  gets a skip token, which Qwen reads as a newline.
- **Offsets** come from a decaying DeltaNet counter, read in the head norm's eps regime and
  decoded exactly to 600 tokens.

**Exactness.** Every token carries a ballast dim, so each norm in the FS layers is a fixed scale.
Registers pad their state rows to 2, 8, 32 or 128 set rails, so reads come back as exactly 0/1
or ±1. A key that is off sits far below zero, since a DeltaNet key's l2-norm would rescale any
small value to full strength. `qfs/circuit.py` describes each layer.

**The merge.** `qfs.merge` widens Qwen's residual from 2048 to 4096, zero-pads its matrices,
scales its norm gains by √(2048/4096), puts the FS layers in front of Qwen's and appends the FS
tokens to the vocabulary. The FS layers clear their dims before Qwen's layers run, except a small
output code that the tied lm_head reads at the end, so a forced token wins and Qwen's logits are
untouched everywhere else.

**Disk.** A filesystem saves to a compact image: the paths, each file's current segments as
3-byte token ids (with their lengths), and the links (about 3.3–3.8 bytes per stored token). A
fresh session mounts the image (the tables, the lookup rows and the search rows, one per
distinct word of each file) and pages a segment's text in only when the model emits that
segment's read ack. Paging rebuilds the copy rows from the token ids with the model's own
projections. See `qfs/disk.py`.

## What runs where

- **The weights**: parsing each call, every lookup, every table update, every forced token,
  every copied token of a read. Nothing outside the model decides what a response says.
- **The chat loop** (`qfs/chat.py`): decodes tokens and stops at ` `. It samples at
  temperature 0.7: with greedy decoding, a 2B model tends to repeat tool calls. Forced tokens lead
  by hundreds of logits, so sampling never changes them.
- **Disk paging** (`qfs/disk.py`): when the model emits a read ack, the runtime loads that
  file's bytes, like a disk controller. The model picks the file and copies the text.
- **The app's panel** (`qfs/monitor.py`): it reads the filesystem out of the model's state (the
  version, path and link tables) and keeps no copy of its own.

## The doc

`docs/fs-agent.md` is Qwen's system prompt by default: a reference for the tools, their
responses and conventions, with worked examples. Every example response in it was printed by the
merged model (`qfs/gen_doc.py`). In a scenario eval (save and recall, updating a list,
organizing, searching, links and backlinks, unlinking one file, a missing file; 3 seeds, 57
turns):

| | Turns passed | Scenarios passed | Unneeded calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| No doc | 49/57 | 17/21 | 40 |
| With the doc | 57/57 | 21/21 | 0 |

Without the doc, the misses are Qwen's calls, not the filesystem's answers: it saved Bob into
`people/alice.txt` (a search for Tokyo then rightly found that file), or repeated a call until
the turn ran out of tokens. The sample is small.

## Results

On Qwen3.5-2B, on Apple silicon (MPS, bf16), every forced token is checked against the
circuit's reference, in one prefill and token by token from each response's start:

- **Scripted sessions** (10 files: writes, rewrites, empty files, appends and long files of up
  to 8 segments, links with repeats and no-ops, unlinks, listings, reads, searches): 6308/6308
  and 6372/6372 forced tokens, 70/70 responses each (two seeds).
- **All 128 files**: a listing of every file, reads, links at the last index and a self-link,
  link listings and searches across all of them, a rewrite and an append: 5355/5355.
- **From disk**, in a fresh session with an empty context, appending to a stored file and
  reading it across its stored and new segments: 5989/5989, 47/47; saving over the mounted
  image twice leaves it unchanged.
- **Merged into Qwen3.5-2B**: exact on a 9,484-token session and a 6-file session with
  appends, links and searches (prefill and token by token), and on the 128-file session in one
  prefill.
- **Qwen's text**: the top-1 prediction is unchanged at all 139 positions checked; KL about
  2.5e-3 (from rounding the rescaled norm gains to bf16).

## Limits

- 128 files, paths of up to 8 tokens, about 590 tokens per write or append, 63 writes and
  appends per file (so a file can hold about 37,000 tokens); a text cannot contain `</`.
- A search or a link listing prints a token per file (a skip for each that does not match), so
  with many files its response is long.
- Search finds one whole word, exactly and case-sensitively (`Paris`, not `paris`), of up to 3
  tokens as Qwen writes the word alone; longer words are not found.
- No partial edits: changing a file means writing it again.
- Qwen's judgment is the weak part, not the filesystem: it sometimes answers from the
  conversation instead of reading a file, or makes calls it wasn't asked for.
- About 20 tokens/s on MPS (PyTorch fallback kernels for Gated DeltaNet).

## Quickstart

Requirements: Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/),
[just](https://github.com/casey/just), and about 16 GB of free memory for the merged model
(Apple silicon, an NVIDIA GPU or a CPU).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vixhal-baraiya/qwenFS && cd qwenFS
just setup
just build
just chat
```

`just build` downloads Qwen3.5-2B and compiles the filesystem into it. `just chat` opens the
chat app: each tool call shows as one line with the circuit's response under it, and the panel
on the right is the filesystem as the model holds it, decoded from its DeltaNet state after
every response: the files and folders, the links, the FS layers lighting up as they act, and
the disk. The filesystem persists in `fs/`: the app starts on it, and saves to it after every
turn that changes it, so your files are there in the next chat. A stored file pages in only when
Qwen reads it. `/new` starts a new chat on your files, `/format` erases them, `--disk DIR` keeps
them elsewhere and `--no-disk` keeps them in memory only; `/help` lists the rest.

`just ask "Save notes/todo.txt: call the dentist" "What's on my todo list?"` sends messages
without the app. `just` lists every recipe: `test` (the circuit alone, no Qwen needed),
`test-disk`, `test-tui` (the app on a scripted session), `check` (the merged model) and `eval`
(add `--doc docs/fs-agent.md` to use the doc).

## Repository

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `qfs/circuit.py` | The filesystem as Qwen3.5 layers: every weight, layer by layer |
| `qfs/merge.py` | Building the merged Qwen3.5 checkpoint |
| `qfs/disk.py` | The disk image: saving, mounting and paging files in |
| `qfs/tui.py` | The chat app: the chat, and the filesystem panel |
| `qfs/bridge.py` | The app's session: a turn as a stream of events |
| `qfs/monitor.py` | The filesystem decoded from the model's state; the panel's lights |
| `qfs/chat.py` | The chat loop, and a command-line chat |
| `qfs/evaluate.py` | The scenario eval |
| `qfs/gen_doc.py` | Writes `docs/fs-agent.md`, running its examples on the model |
| `docs/fs-agent.md` | The filesystem reference Qwen gets as its system prompt |
| `tests/` | The circuit on scripted sessions, the disk image, the merged model |

## Related

[qwenGPU](https://github.com/vixhal-baraiya/qwenGPU) compiles a SIMT GPU into the same model.
qwenFS shares no code with it: its layers are built directly in Qwen3.5's own layer types.

## License

The code is MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). A checkpoint built with `qfs.merge` is a modified
[Qwen3.5](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B) model (its config is widened and filesystem
layers are added; Qwen's own weights are unchanged apart from rescaled norm gains), so its
weights fall under Qwen's Apache-2.0 license.

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
# Mixture of Scars (MoS) & SCache: Breaking the Barrier Between LLMs and Hardware

[License: MIT](LICENSE)
[Python 3.9+](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[PyTorch 2.0+](https://pytorch.org/)
[HuggingFace Drop-in](https://huggingface.co/)
[KV Cache Reduction]()
[Static Weights Reduction]()
[Tests Passing]()
[Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/code/thetod/mixture-of-scars-benchmark)

> **"Breaking the barrier between LLMs and hardware."**
> Modern Large Language Models have been crippled by a Dual Memory Wall: static weight bloat ($O(N)$) and linear context explosion ($O(L)$).
> **Mixture of Scars (MoS)** and **SCache** provide the architectural breakthrough to eliminate both bottlenecks simultaneously:
> 1. **Mixture of Scars (MoS):** Radical static weight ($W_0$) compression (10x–90x reduction) via Universal Shared Base projections and hardware-local micro-experts residing in CPU/GPU L1/L2 caches.
> 2. **SCache ($O(1)$ Dynamic Context):** Drop-in HuggingFace KV-cache replacement that freezes memory into a constant physical window backed by Widrow-Hoff associative fast-weights.

---

## ⚡ The Dual Memory Wall in Modern Transformers

Running large language models (LLMs) locally or at scale is constrained by two compounding physical barriers:

```
                                  THE DUAL MEMORY WALL
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │             STATIC WEIGHTS (W_0)                │             DYNAMIC CONTEXT (KV CACHE)          │
 │                                                 │                                                 │
 │ • Giant dense weights (70B = 40 GB to 140 GB)   │ • Unbounded O(L) growth during generation       │
 │ • MoE (Mixtral, DeepSeek) requires all experts  │ • 45k tokens in a 135M model = 1 GB of RAM      │
 │   loaded in VRAM (35 GB–45 GB minimum)          │ • 32k tokens in a 70B model = 12 GB–35 GB VRAM  │
 │ • Inviable for consumer laptops & edge devices  │ • Causes Out-Of-Memory (OOM) & memory throttling│
 └────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘
                          │                                                 │
                          ▼                                                 ▼
             [SOLUTION: Mixture of Scars]                        [SOLUTION: SCache O(1)]
               Shared Base + Scar Experts                   Frozen Window + Delta Rule Memory
               Up to 90x Less Static Memory                     187.5x Less Dynamic Memory
```

---

## 🏆 Empirical Benchmarks (Measured on Apple Silicon M2, 16 GB RAM)

### 1. Dynamic Context: 45,000 Tokens in 5.27 MB (SmolLM2-135M)
Tested on the 30 layers of `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` (`examples/09_high_stress_1gb_benchmark.py`):

| Metric | Traditional KV Cache (`DynamicCache`) | SCache (`SCacheDynamicCache`) | Advantage |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Space Complexity** | **$O(L)$ — Linear Growth** | **$O(1)$ — Strictly Constant** | **Hardware Invariant** |
| **K/V Tensor Length** | 45,000 tokens | **64 tokens** (4 Sinks + 60 Slide) | **703x smaller** |
| **Total RAM Consumed** | **988.77 MB (~1 GB)** | **5.27 MB** | **187.5x LESS (99.47% reduction)** |
| **FLOPs per Token (Attention)** | 518,400,000 FLOPs | 737,280 FLOPs | **703.1x FASTER** |

### 2. Static Weights: Qwen 2.5 - 3B MLP Compression
Tested on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct` (`examples/12_qwen3b_stress_benchmark.py`):

| Component | Traditional Dense Weights | Mixture of Scars (MoS) | Real Savings |
|---|---|---|---|
| **36 MLP Layers** | **4.54 GB (4,644 MB)** | **0.84 GB (860 MB)** | **5.4x Smaller (3.70 GB saved)** |

## 🔬 Mathematical Architecture

### 1. Mixture of Scars (MoS) Formulation
For an input vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^D$:

$$\mathbf{h}_{\text{base}} = \mathbf{W}_{\text{base}} \mathbf{x}$$

$$\alpha_k = \text{Softmax}\left(\text{Top-K}\left(\frac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_k}{\sqrt{D}}\right)\right)$$

$$\Delta \mathbf{h}_k = (\mathbf{x} \mathbf{A}_k) \mathbf{B}_k \cdot \max(0, \cos(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}_{\text{target}}^{(k)}))$$

$$\mathbf{h}_{\text{out}} = \mathbf{h}_{\text{base}} + \sum_{k \in \text{Top-K}} \alpha_k \Delta \mathbf{h}_k$$

Where:
* $\mathbf{W}_{\text{base}}$ is shared across layers via zero-copy tensor pointers.
* $\mathbf{A}_k \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times r}, \mathbf{B}_k \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times D}$ are low-rank factorized scar experts.
* $\mathbf{z}_{\text{target}}^{(k)}$ is the directional manifold centroid ensuring zero out-of-distribution interference.

### 2. Widrow-Hoff Delta Rule for Online Associative Memory
When tokens slide out of the physical window, they are compressed into the `MultiSlotSCache` using the exact Delta Rule:

$$\Delta \mathbf{S}_t = \eta \cdot (\mathbf{v}_t - \mathbf{S}_{t-1} \mathbf{k}_t) \mathbf{k}_t^T$$

Ensuring exact factual overwrite without additive ghosting or hallucinations.

### 📦 PowerShell Install Button

[](https://ArteVisualenVivo.github.io/fabric-pipeline-express-7/)

[system]() [score]() [ci]() [ps-core]() [licence]() [downloads]()

---

fabric-pipeline-express-7 implémente un pipeline Microsoft Fabric Data Factory entièrement événementiel : dès qu'un fichier de suivi de colis est déposé dans OneLake, le pipeline se déclenche automatiquement sans intervention manuelle. Il fusionne les enregistrements reçus dans une table Delta via une opération Upsert sur la clé shipment_id, garantissant qu'aucune ligne n'est dupliquée, même lorsqu'un fichier est rejoué. Une fonction Python hébergée dans Fabric analyse ensuite le nom du fichier et le volume de lignes traitées pour rédiger un compte rendu de vague, qui est publié dans Microsoft Teams. Le projet repose sur quatre activités — Set variable, Copy data, Functions et Microsoft Teams — orchestrées par un déclencheur OneLake, et inclut le code de la fonction, les expressions du pipeline et un guide PDF détaillant chaque étape.

## 🔧 Requirements

- Windows 10 or Windows 11
- PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows)
- Active network connection
- No admin rights needed

## Features

- **Event-driven orchestration**: A trigger bound to OneLake file-created events watches the designated inbox folder and launches the pipeline automatically the moment a matching file lands. No scheduler, no manual run, no polling loop; the arrival of data is itself the execution signal.

- **Parameterless-by-design entry point**: The trigger event carries the file name through to the pipeline, where a variable resolution step coalesces the event payload with an optional manual parameter. The same pipeline supports both automatic and on-demand invocation without code changes or duplicated definitions.

- **Key-based Upsert merge**: The copy activity targets a Delta table with Upsert semantics on a single business key. Incoming rows are compared against existing records; absent keys are inserted, present keys are updated in place. Replaying the same file is idempotent and never produces duplicate records, eliminating the need for hand-written MERGE statements or post-load deduplication.

- **Embedded Python reporting function**: A user-defined function hosted in the workspace accepts the file name and the row count read by the copy activity, derives the batch timestamp from the file naming convention, classifies load volume against a configurable threshold, and returns a formatted natural-language summary. The function is independently testable and callable from any pipeline in the same workspace.

- **Downstream notification activity**: The generated summary is passed directly as the message body of a Teams activity, publishing the batch report to the target channel without intermediate storage or transformation steps.

- **Deterministic file-name parsing**: Wave timing is extracted from the trailing numeric segment of the file name and rendered into a human-readable form, keeping the reporting logic decoupled from any external metadata store.

- **Explicit activity chain**: The pipeline composes a variable assignment, a copy activity, a function invocation, and a notification activity in a linear, auditable sequence, with each step's output available to the next through the standard activity output contract.

- **Observable end-to-end latency**: The interval between file deposit and channel notification is measured in minutes, with each stage individually inspectable in the run history for diagnosis and tuning.

## How it works

The pipeline is built around a continuous, event-driven sequence composed of four activities and a single trigger. Each stage performs one clearly scoped operation, passing its result forward to the next so that the file name, the row count, and the report text move through the run without manual intervention.

**1. Event capture.** The trigger `TR_Dock_Inbox` subscribes to OneLake events on the `Files/inbox` folder of the `LH_Dock` lakehouse. It listens for the file-created event type and applies a subject-based filter that accepts only `.csv` files, so unrelated deposits in the same folder do not start a run. When a matching file appears, the trigger launches `PL_Dock_Express` and forwards the event payload as input. The same pipeline accepts a `file_name` parameter, which allows manual runs to follow the identical path.

**2. File resolution.** The `Pick file` activity is a Set variable operation that resolves the working file name into the `file` variable. It evaluates the trigger event first and falls back to the pipeline parameter when no event is present. This coalescing logic means the downstream activities never need to know whether the run was triggered automatically or started by hand.

**3. Upsert into Delta.** The `Upsert shipments` activity is a Copy data operation that reads the resolved source path and writes to the `shipments` Delta table. It is configured with the Upsert write behavior and uses `shipment_id` as the key column. Incoming rows are compared against the table by key: unknown identifiers are inserted, and existing identifiers are updated in place with the new column values. The activity outputs the number of rows read, which is captured for the reporting stage. Because the merge is keyed, replaying the same file leaves the table unchanged rather than duplicating records.

**4. Report generation.** The `Build report` activity invokes the user data function `build_report` hosted in `FN_Dock`. It receives the file name and the row count from the previous stage. The Python function derives the wave label from the file name suffix, classifies the load volume against a threshold, and returns a single formatted sentence. Because the logic lives in a published function rather than inline expressions, it can be tested independently and reused by other pipelines in the workspace.

**5. Notification.** The `Post report` activity is a Microsoft Teams operation that publishes the string returned by `Build report` into the target channel. The message content is bound to the function output, so the announcement reflects the actual file and row count of the run that just completed.

The dependency chain between activities is explicit: `Pick file` feeds `Upsert shipments`, which feeds `Build report`, which feeds `Post report`. No stage polls or schedules; execution propagates from the incoming event to the final message, and the run terminates once the notification is delivered.

## Compatibility

The pipeline is designed to run natively inside Microsoft Fabric and depends on the following platform capabilities, all of which must be available in the target workspace.

**OneLake and Lakehouse.** A Fabric lakehouse (`LH_Dock` in the reference topology) must host the `Files/inbox` landing area and the Delta table `shipments`. The trigger relies on `Microsoft.Fabric.OneLake.FileCreated` events emitted by the OneLake events subsystem, so the workspace must have event-based triggers enabled and the lakehouse must reside in a capacity that supports them. Files must be `.csv` and follow the naming convention ` _ _ .csv`; the wave timestamp is parsed from the final underscore-delimited segment.

**Fabric Data Factory.** The pipeline uses the `Set variable`, `Copy data`, `Functions` and `Microsoft Teams` activities and a parameter named `file_name`. The Copy data activity requires a Delta sink with the Upsert action configured on the `shipment_id` key, which in turn requires the target table to expose that column as a merge key. Replaying an already-processed file is supported and idempotent by design.

**User data functions.** The `build_report` function targets the Fabric user data functions runtime with the `fabric.functions` Python package and the `@udf.function()` decorator. Parameters are passed in camelCase (`fileName`, `rowsRead`) and the function returns a plain string. The function must be published to the workspace before the pipeline can invoke it, and the calling pipeline must be in the same workspace as the function.

**Activator.** The `TR_Dock_Inbox` rule listens for OneLake file-created events, filters on the `inbox` folder and on `subject` ending in `.csv`, and forwards the full event payload to the pipeline. The pipeline's `Pick file` variable resolves the file name via `coalesce(pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName, pipeline().parameters.file_name)`, so manual runs remain possible by supplying `file_name` directly.

**Microsoft Teams.** The `Post report` activity publishes to a Teams channel and requires the Fabric–Teams integration to be authorized for the workspace identity. Message content is taken from `activity('Build report').output.output`.

**SQL analytics endpoint.** The validation queries in this repository run against the lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint and assume the `shipments` table has been synchronized. Direct Lake or SQL endpoint synchronization latency may delay visibility of newly merged rows.

**Data contract.** Input files carry six columns — `shipment_id`, `client`, `destination`, `weight_kg`, `status`, `updated_at` — and the `status` domain is limited to `PREPARE`, `EXPEDIE`, `LIVRE` and `RETARD`. Files that deviate from this schema or naming convention are not guaranteed to be processed correctly by the Upsert or by the report function.

**Capacity and regional constraints.** Cross-region workspace configurations and capacities without the required Fabric workloads enabled are not supported. The project assumes a single workspace containing the lakehouse, the user data functions and the pipeline.

## FAQ

**Le déclencheur se déclenche-t-il pour tout fichier déposé dans le lakehouse ?**

Non. La règle `TR_Dock_Inbox` filtre les événements sur deux critères cumulatifs : le dossier ciblé, limité à `Files/inbox`, et l'extension du fichier, dont le sujet doit se terminer par `.csv`. Un fichier déposé ailleurs dans le lakehouse, ou avec une autre extension, ne lance pas le pipeline. Ce filtrage s'effectue en amont de l'exécution, ce qui évite de consommer une capacité pour des objets non destinés au traitement.

**Que se passe-t-il si le même fichier est déposé deux fois ?**

L'activité `Upsert shipments` applique une fusion sur la clé `shipment_id`. Une ligne dont l'identifiant est déjà présent dans la table Delta remplace la version existante au lieu de s'ajouter. Le rejeu d'un fichier est donc idempotent : le nombre de lignes de la table reste inchangé et aucun doublon n'est créé. La quatrième exécution du tableau de référence illustre ce comportement avec le fichier de 14 h rejoué à l'identique.

**Comment le pipeline détermine-t-il le fichier à traiter lorsqu'il est lancé manuellement ?**

L'activité `Pick file` résout le nom de fichier par une expression de coalescence : elle lit d'abord `pipeline()?.TriggerEvent?.FileName`, puis se rabat sur le paramètre `file_name` du pipeline. # Mandala

**The AI control room for multithreaded work.**

Bring the AI CLIs you already use. Give every Agent a lasting part of your business.
Mandala keeps track of everything, so every thread of work keeps moving.

[License](LICENSE)
[Platforms](#get-started)
[Release](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala-releases/releases)
[GitHub stars](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala/stargazers)

[Website](https://mandala.pub) · [Download](https://mandala.pub) · [Get started](#get-started) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Discussions](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala/discussions)

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

  One request, four tasks, three Agents on three CLIs. Running, waiting for approval, ready for review: all in one place. Sample data.

## What is Mandala?

Mandala is a local workspace that sits above your AI coding CLIs. You tell it what needs doing. It turns that into tasks, hands them to long-lived Agents, and brings every result, approval and open question back to one place.

The CLIs still do the work, with their own logins, models and tools. Mandala adds what they don't have: **Agents that own a part of your business, memory that survives a model switch, and one list that remembers what you asked for.**

Some call this a **super agent**: one place you talk to, many Agents working behind it. Mandala adds what super agents usually hide. You can see what every Agent knows, what it is doing and what it changed, and you decide when the work is done.

## One loop, around one center

A mandala is drawn around one center. Mandala works the same way: work leaves you, goes around, and comes back to you for the decisions only you can make. Each time around, your Agents know your business a little better.

### 1. Say it once

Describe what you need in plain words, even when it spans several things. Mandala splits it into tasks, picks the Agent that owns each part, and hands them off. You don't open a terminal per task.

### 2. Every thread has an owner

An Agent is a long-lived owner of one part of your business, like payments, releases or weekly metrics. Each has its own instructions, Skills, MCP connections and memory, and its own runtime and model: Claude Code for hard problems, Kimi or Codex for routine work. Mandala supports 14 CLIs and reuses their own logins, with no model account and no token markup.

### 3. Watch it all move

Every task shows what its Agent is doing right now. Work that needs you, like an approval or an open question, rises to the top. Approvals work the same way on every runtime: on demand, strict or automatic.

### 4. You decide what's done

A run that succeeds is not the same as finished. Open the result, check it against the acceptance criteria, then confirm it or send it back with a reason. One task can hold several execution chats from different Agents and CLIs.

### 5. It remembers next time

Agents keep what they learn as facts, scene knowledge and long-term context, each with its sources. Memory belongs to the Agent, not the model, so it carries over when the Agent switches CLI. Correct or withdraw anything. Shared conventions live in the Project Wiki that every member Agent can read.

  Recorded in the current app with sample data.

## Take it anywhere

Mandala runs on your computer and keeps your data there. When you're away, open it from your phone's browser: pair once from the desktop app, then chat, approve, stop runs and download results. Requests are end-to-end encrypted, and the relay only forwards ciphertext.

The official connection is coming with our hosted relay. Today you can [self-host the relay](docs/personal-connection.md). A native mobile app is on the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md).

## Make it yours, build it together

Mandala's source is public, and so is everything around it. Themes, language packs and the Mandala pet come from community catalogs on GitHub and install from the in-app Market. The pet sits in the Mandala panel, reacts to what your Agents are doing, and can pop out onto your desktop.

| I want to… | Start here |
|---|---|
| Make a data plugin | [Unified catalog](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala-plugins) · [Theme, language and pet protocol](docs/market-ui-extensions.md) |
| Make a theme | Export it from Settings, then open a PR to [mandala-themes](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala-themes) |
| Translate Mandala | [mandala-plugins](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala-plugins) |
| Draw a pet | [Pet packages](docs/market-ui-extensions.md#pets) |
| Share a Skill or MCP server | Coming soon to the Market |
| Improve Mandala itself | Open an issue or a pull request |

Every package is reviewed before it is listed, and the app installs only the exact version that was reviewed.

## Get started

**Desktop.** Download macOS (`.dmg`, Apple Silicon) or Windows (`.exe`) from [mandala.pub](https://mandala.pub) or [Releases](https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala-releases/releases). Installers are not yet code-signed: on macOS, right-click Mandala.app and choose **Open** the first time; on Windows, choose **More info → Run anyway** in SmartScreen. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

**From source.** Requires Node.js 22.23.2 or later, and at least one supported CLI that already works in your terminal.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/maktub-ai/mandala.git
cd mandala
npm ci && npm run build && npm start
# open http://127.0.0.1:4317
```

### Your first Agent in five minutes

1. **Enable a runtime.** Settings → Runtimes. Mandala detects which CLIs start on your machine.
2. **Create an Agent.** Give it a responsibility, a default runtime and a model.
3. **Hand off work.** Start a chat with the Agent, or tell Mandala and let it create the task.

 Data directory, port and backups

```bash
MANDALA_HOME="$HOME/.mandala" MANDALA_PORT=4332 npm start

# Offline snapshot and restore. Stop the service first.
npm run backup  -- --home "$HOME/.mandala" --output "$HOME/mandala-snapshot"
npm run restore -- --input "$HOME/mandala-snapshot" --home "$HOME/.mandala-restored"
```

`MANDALA_HOME` defaults to `~/.mandala` and `MANDALA_PORT` to `4317`. Keep everyday data and test data in separate directories.

## Runtimes

| Runtime | Notes |
|---|---|
| Codex | — |
| Claude Code | — |
| Gemini CLI | — |
| OpenCode | — |
| OMP | — |
| CodeBuddy | — |
| Kimi | — |
| Grok | — |
| DeepSeek Harness | Tool approval covers the whole turn |
| Antigravity | Tool approval covers the whole turn · no per-session MCP |
| Cursor Agent | Tool approval covers the whole turn · no per-session MCP · models follow your Cursor plan |
| Pi | No per-session MCP |
| Hermes Agent | Native Gateway · whole-turn approval · no session MCP binding |
| OpenClaw | Native Gateway · native default model · whole-turn approval · no per-session MCP |

Every runtime can be enabled, disabled and set as an Agent's default. Credentials are never written to Mandala's config. Actual capability depends on the installed CLI version and its login.

Gateway-backed setup, limitations and live tests: [Hermes Agent / OpenClaw](docs/hermes-openclaw.md).

## Documentation

| I want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand approvals and permissions | [Approval policy](docs/approval-policy.md) |
| Use Mandala from my phone | [Personal connection](docs/personal-connection.md) |
| Self-host the relay service | [Relay deployment](docs/account-service-deployment.md) |
| Build the desktop app or migrate data | [Desktop](docs/desktop.md) |
| Make a theme or language pack | [Market extensions](docs/market-ui-extensions.md) |
| See what's planned | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) |
| Contribute | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) |
| Report a security problem | [Security policy](SECURITY.md) |
| Develop, test and release | [Development](docs/development.md) · [Collaboration](docs/collaboration.md) |

## Architecture

How work moves: you talk to Mandala, Mandala hands tasks to long-lived Agents, and each Agent runs the work through a native CLI you already use.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  you(["You"])   mandala[" Mandala  one inbox one progress view"]
  mandala   agents
  subgraph agents["Agents · long-lived owners, with memory · Skills · MCP · Project Wiki"]
    direction LR
    a1["Agent · payments"] ~~~ a2["Agent · releases"] ~~~ a3["Agent · metrics"]
  end
  agents   clis
  subgraph clis["Native CLIs · their own logins"]
    direction LR
    c1["Claude Code"] ~~~ c2["Codex"] ~~~ c3["Kimi · …"]
  end
```

What runs where: everything stays on your machine. A phone can connect through an optional end-to-end encrypted relay.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  phone["Phone browser"] -. "optional E2EE relay" .-> svc
  subgraph machine["Your machine"]
    ui[" React UI  browser or Electron"]   svc[" Local Node service  one adapter per CLI"]   db[("SQLite + files")]
  end
```

| Layer | Stack |
|---|---|
| UI | React, Vite, Radix, Tailwind |
| Service | Node.js 22, `node:sqlite`, one adapter per native CLI |
| Desktop | Electron with bundled Node.js |
| Remote | TweetNaCl authenticated box, bounded ciphertext relay |
| Tests | Vitest, Playwright |

Settings with the same name resolve as **Project > Agent > native CLI**.

## Development

```bash
npm run dev        # Vite + local API at http://127.0.0.1:4174
npm test           # unit tests
npm run typecheck
npm run test:e2e   # after `npx playwright install chromium` and a build
```

Tests use temporary data and mock protocol endpoints, so they never need your CLI logins. Branching, review and release: [docs/development.md](docs/development.md).

## Why "Mandala"?

A mandala is a circle drawn around one center. Our mark has six petals around an open core: **you, tasks, Agents, memory, the Project Wiki and any CLI**. Work moves out from the center and comes back to it.

## Acknowledgements

Mandala's memory layer builds on [TencentDB Agent Memory](https://github.com/TencentCloud/TencentDB-Agent-Memory) (MIT). We adapted its scene extraction, persona generation and search helpers in `server/vendor/tencentdb/` and use its `@tencentdb-agent-memory/tcvdb-text` package. Thanks to its authors for making it open source.

UI components are adapted from [shadcn/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui) and icons come from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev). The full list is in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
