# CodeSlice

> Read any codebase. Ask questions as you go. Get answers you can verify.

CodeSlice 是一款本地优先的 AI 代码阅读桌面应用。添加代码仓库后，打开文件、选中代码并开始提问。回答附有可点击的文件与行号引用；AI 需要写文件或运行命令时，先由你审核授权。

**CodeSlice** is a local-first AI code-reading desktop app for developers. Drop
in a repository, open a source file, select the code you want to understand, and
start a conversation. Answers include clickable file-and-line citations; changes
and shell commands require your approval before they run.

**[Download CodeSlice for Windows](https://github.com/ctianye/CodeSlice/releases/latest)** ·
[Browse all releases](https://github.com/ctianye/CodeSlice/releases) ·
[MIT license](LICENSE)

CodeSlice project picker and local project list

## See CodeSlice in action

### Read a repository while asking questions about it

Open a project, browse its file tree, and read the source in the integrated
editor. Ask a question in the conversation pane or select a few lines to focus
the conversation on that code.

Browse and read source code in the CodeSlice desktop app

### Follow answers back to the source

CodeSlice returns citations with its answers. Select a file-and-line reference
to navigate directly to the relevant source code.

An AI answer with clickable source-code citations

### Stay in control of changes and commands

When an agent requests a file write or command, inspect the request and approve
or reject it. Approval is required before the operation runs.

Review and approve an AI-requested file change

### Keep reading notes close to the code

Save useful explanations as searchable notes. Code references in a note take
you back to the original source.

Browse saved CodeSlice knowledge-base notes

## Getting started

1. Download `CodeSlice-0.1.0-Setup.exe` from the [latest GitHub Release](https://github.com/ctianye/CodeSlice/releases/latest) and install it on Windows 10 or 11.
2. Start CodeSlice and add a local repository by selecting its folder.
3. Open a source file, select the code you want to understand, and ask a question in the conversation pane.
4. Open **Settings → Model** to configure a compatible model provider and API key. The key is stored in Windows Credential Manager.
5. Save useful answers as notes. Review and explicitly approve each proposed file write or shell command.

The application, repository index, and saved conversations run and stay on your
computer. When you ask a model a question, CodeSlice sends the relevant question
and code context to the model provider configured by you; that provider's data
handling policies apply. API keys are saved in Windows Credential Manager.

## What it does

- Reads local repositories in a three-pane file tree, source editor, and chat.
- Splits supported languages into structural chunks using Tree-sitter and
  searches with local FTS5 and vector similarity retrieval.
- Adds navigable file-and-line citations to answers.
- Requires per-action approval before writing a file or running a command.
- Turns conversations into indexed, searchable notes that can be reused across
  projects.
- Saves conversations, indexes, and application data locally.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) or Windows 11.
- A compatible model provider and your own API key for AI answers. Local model
  providers are supported where configured.

The installer includes the desktop app and local Python backend. End users do
not need to install Python, Node.js, or developer tools.

## Known limitations

- Windows is the packaged desktop platform for the first release.
- Model responses require a configured provider; API charges and provider
  retention policies depend on your provider and plan.
- Tree-sitter structural indexing is currently configured for Python,
  TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, JSON, and Bash. Other files
  remain available for the application’s supported text-based workflows.

## For contributors

See [local development](#本地开发), [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), and
[packaging](packaging/README.md). The backend tests run with `uv run pytest` from
`backend/`. Build a release installer with
`pwsh -File packaging/build_backend.ps1` followed by
`pwsh -File packaging/build_desktop.ps1` on a configured Windows build machine.

Contributions and issue reports are welcome. For changes to the application,
please explain the problem, reproduction steps, and expected behavior.

> 本地优先的「代码阅读」智能体桌面应用。把任意一个代码仓库拖进来，边读边问，
> 每个回答都带可点击的文件/行号引用；需要动文件或跑命令时，逐条向你申请授权。

CodeSlice 是一个跑在你机器上的 Electron 桌面程序 + 本地 Python 服务。
模型调用走你自己的 API Key，代码、索引、对话记录全部留在本地
（安装版在 `%APPDATA%\codeslice-desktop`，见[数据与凭据](#数据与凭据)），
不上传任何服务器。

## 目录

- [核心特性](#核心特性)
- [架构](#架构)
- [技术栈](#技术栈)
- [仓库结构](#仓库结构)

- [安全模型](#安全模型)
- [V1 范围与路线图](#v1-范围与路线图)
- [常见问题](#常见问题)

---

## 核心特性

| 能力 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| **边读边问** | 三段式界面：文件树 / 代码（Monaco）/ 对话。选中代码即可提问，回答锚定在具体行。 |
| **多标签编辑器** | 像 VS Code 那样同时开多个文件和笔记，标签可拖拽排序、中键或 × 关闭、右键「关闭其他」。点笔记里的引用会新开一个代码标签，原来的笔记不会消失。 |
| **集成终端** | 编辑器下方可展开的终端，直接跑命令；输出逐行流式到达，可拖拽调高、↑↓ 翻历史。 |
| **AI 可执行命令** | 对话里模型调 `run_command` 走的审批卡与终端是同一套沙箱：同一份危险命令黑名单，同一条 `command_rules` 授权规则。 |
| **可溯源的引用** | 每条回答附 `文件:行号` 引用块，点击直接跳转并用左侧色条标出范围；再点同一个引用块取消标亮。 |
| **混合检索** | SQLite FTS5 关键词检索 + numpy 余弦相似度语义检索，结果融合排序。 |
| **结构化索引** | Tree-sitter 解析 Python / TS / JS / Go / Rust / Java / C / C++ / JSON / Bash，按函数、类、模块切块。 |
| **逐条授权** | 写文件、执行命令必须经你批准，规则可设为「仅本次 / 本会话 / 总是」。没有「信任整个项目」一键放行。 |
| **代码锚点** | 笔记与引用绑定到代码位置；文件改动后自动标记为 `modified` / `moved` / `deleted`。 |
| **笔记入知识库** | 对话里一键把回答整理成固定模板笔记，自动进入检索管道可被再次引用，并可导出为 `.md`。知识库跨项目：一个面板看全部项目的笔记，可按任意层级的文件夹归档（`note_folders` 自引用树）。 |
| **代码对话卡** | 打开文件时，编辑器上方列出这个文件上的片段对话；鼠标悬停高亮对应行，点击回到那段对话。 |
| **只讲选中的代码** | 片段对话默认只看选中的那一段，不主动去别处读文件；需要周边信息时在输入框打开「联系上下文」。 |
| **按行提问** | 点行号选整行，再点别处继续累加、点同一行取消，「就这些行提问」把这一组行当作上下文。 |
| **对话分区** | 侧栏把「本项目对话」置顶、「其他对话」折叠在下，列表项标注来自哪个项目。 |
| **索引状态自检** | 打开项目即检查索引：从未索引时静默建立，已索引则静默增量刷新，无需手动操作；工具栏常驻「309 文件 · 1508 片段」累计徽标。 |
| **知识点标题** | 对话与笔记的标题由回答内容概括（「多轮对话消息两种写法」），不再是「关于 README.md 第 357-359 行」。 |
| **本地凭据** | API Key 存 Windows 凭据管理器，绝不写进 SQLite。 |

---

## 架构

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Electron 主进程 (desktop/)                                 │
│  · 启动后端子进程，读取 stdout 的握手行获取端口 + Token      │
│  · 通过 preload 把 apiBase / token 注入渲染进程             │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                │ BrowserWindow           │ spawn
                ▼                         ▼
┌───────────────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ 渲染进程 (frontend/)       │   │ 本地服务 (backend/)             │
│ React 18 + TS + Monaco     │──▶│ FastAPI + Uvicorn              │
│ · 文件树 / 代码 / 对话     │HTTP│ · 127.0.0.1:           │
│ · SSE 流式对话             │SSE │ · X-Session-Token 鉴权          │
│ · 授权卡片                 │   │ · LangGraph 智能体编排          │
└───────────────────────────┘   └───────────┬─────────────────────┘
                                            │
                    ┌───────────────────────┼────────────────────┐
                    ▼                       ▼                    ▼
            ┌───────────────┐      ┌────────────────┐   ┌────────────────┐
            │ SQLite        │      │ Tree-sitter    │   │ 模型 API       │
            │ · 业务表       │      │ · 结构化切块    │   │ OpenAI 兼容 /  │
            │ · FTS5 全文    │      │ · 函数/类边界   │   │ Anthropic      │
            │ · 向量 (BLOB)  │      └────────────────┘   └────────────────┘
            │ · LangGraph    │
            │   checkpoint   │
            └───────────────┘
```

**启动握手**：后端在真正开始监听之后，向 stdout 打印一行

```
CODESLICE_READY {"port": 54746, "token": "xN-Nxo...", "version": "0.1.0"}
```

Electron 主进程读到这一行才知道该连哪个端口、用什么 Token。
`CODESLICE_PORT=0` 时端口由内核分配，因此安装版不会出现端口冲突。

---

## 技术栈

| 层 | 技术 | 选型理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 桌面壳 | Electron + electron-builder (NSIS) | 需要管理子进程、原生文件对话框、系统凭据 |
| 界面 | React 18 + TypeScript + Vite 5 | 成熟的编辑器周边生态，构建快 |
| 代码显示 | Monaco Editor | 与 VS Code 同源，语法高亮与 diff 开箱即用 |
| API | FastAPI + Uvicorn | 原生 async、SSE 简单、Pydantic 校验 |
| 智能体 | LangGraph + LangChain Core | 显式状态图，中断/恢复（人工审批）是一等公民 |
| 模型接入 | `langchain-openai` / `langchain-anthropic` | 协议由用户显式选择，不做协议嗅探 |
| 存储 | SQLite（WAL）+ FTS5 | 零运维、单文件、可随应用一起搬运 |
| 向量检索 | numpy 余弦相似度 | V1 规模（万级 chunk）足够，且可替换成任意 VectorStore |
| 语法分析 | Tree-sitter + 逐语言 grammar 包 | 增量解析、跨语言、无需语言服务器 |
| 凭据 | `keyring`（Windows Credential Manager） | 交给操作系统保管，不落盘明文 |

---

```

├── backend/                  # 本地 Python 服务
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── main.py           # FastAPI 入口 + CODESLICE_READY 握手
│   │   ├── api/              # 路由：projects / indexing / conversations / notes / terminal ...
│   │   ├── agent/            # LangGraph 图、工具、prompts、checkpoint、节点配置

│   │   ├── indexing/         # 语言识别、Tree-sitter 切块、索引器
│   │   ├── models/           # 模型适配器、embedding
│   │   ├── retrieval/        # 关键词 + 语义混合检索
│   │   ├── services/         # 路径校验、git、锚点、终端沙箱、命令执行
│   │   └── storage/          # 数据访问层
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   ├── scripts/              # smoke / e2e_contract / ui_smoke / mock_model / cdp_reload 联调脚本
```

---

## 本地开发

**前置**：Windows 10/11、Python 3.11、[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)、Node.js 24、npm。

### 一键启动

```powershell
pwsh -File scripts\dev.ps1
```

脚本会：固定 `CODESLICE_TOKEN=dev-token` 与端口 8000 → `uv sync` → 在独立窗口启动后端
→ 轮询 `/api/health` 直到就绪 → 启动 `desktop/npm run dev`。

### 分步启动

三个终端依次执行：

```powershell
# 1) 后端 —— http://127.0.0.1:8000
cd backend
uv sync
$env:CODESLICE_TOKEN = "dev-token"   # 可选：固定 Token，默认每次启动随机
uv run fastapi dev app/main.py --port 8000
```

> `fastapi dev` 有自己的 `--port` 参数，它不会读取 `CODESLICE_PORT` 环境变量
> （那个变量只在直接运行打包后的 `codeslice-backend.exe` 时生效）。

```powershell
# 2) 渲染进程（浏览器调试用）—— http://localhost:3000
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

```powershell
# 3) 桌面壳（会加载 1) 和 2)）
cd desktop
npm install
npm run dev
```

后端启动后，`GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health` 可直接验证；交互式文档在
`/api/docs`。所有 `/api/*` 请求都需要 `X-Session-Token` 头（仅 `/api/health` 豁免）。

浏览器模式下（没有 Electron 注入 Token），可在界面里手动粘贴 Token，或写入
`frontend/.env.local`：

```
VITE_SESSION_TOKEN=dev-token
```

桌面壳在开发模式下从 `CODESLICE_SESSION_TOKEN` 读取 Token（`scripts\dev.ps1` 会同时
设置它与 `CODESLICE_TOKEN`）。若手动分步启动，需自行设置：

```powershell
$env:CODESLICE_SESSION_TOKEN = "dev-token"
$env:CODESLICE_DEV_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:3000"   # 可选，默认就是这个
cd desktop; npm run dev
```

---

## 构建与打包

```powershell
# 1) 后端 → packaging\dist-backend\codeslice-backend.exe（扁平布局）
pwsh -File packaging\build_backend.ps1

# 2) 前端 + Electron → desktop\release\CodeSlice-0.1.0-Setup.exe
pwsh -File packaging\build_desktop.ps1
```

第一步会额外跑自检与冒烟测试（真实启动 exe、握手、调 `/api/health`、验证未授权请求

# 🩺 AI Healthcare Data Lakehouse & Clinical Intelligence Platform
### *Production Databricks Medallion Lakehouse, PySpark Distributed ETL, Delta Lake 4.x Liquid Clustering, SCD Type 2 & Multi-Agent RAG Platform*

   

   

   

---

## 💡 Executive Overview & Architecture Value Proposition

Processing multimodal Electronic Health Records (EHRs), continuous bedside ICU telemetry, and epidemiological cohorts across disparate hospital silos creates severe data latency, schema drift, and diagnostic bottlenecks.

**AI Healthcare Data Lakehouse & Clinical Intelligence Platform** is a distributed data platform and clinical decision support system. Engineered around a **Databricks Unity Catalog Medallion Lakehouse (Bronze, Silver, Gold)**, it ingests and processes **1.5M+ complex patient event records** using **PySpark 4.3 (Apache Spark 4.3.0)**, **Parquet 2.0 (Format v2)**, and **Delta Lake 4.x**.

### Core Engineering Proof Points:
* **Delta Lake 4.x Liquid Clustering (`clusterBy`)**: Replaced static partitioning with dynamic multidimensional clustering on high-cardinality keys (`patient_id`, `event_timestamp`), cutting table **`MERGE` rewrite runtime by 50% (from 12 to 6 minutes)**.
* **SCD Type 2 Historical Dimension Tracking**: Implements temporal versioning on the clinical patient dimension (`is_current`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`), guaranteeing point-in-time auditing with zero data leakage.
* **Apache Airflow & Databricks Lakeflow Orchestration**: End-to-end automated DAGs with Spark Declarative Pipeline data expectation contracts routing malformed records to partitioned quarantine dead-letter queues.
* **Sub-100ms Multi-Agent RAG**: High-throughput semantic retrieval pipeline integrating distributed embeddings, local vector caching, and semantic deduplication, compressing context payloads by **70%** under sub-100ms response SLAs.
* **Database Plan Optimization**: Engineered composite B-tree indexes and query execution plan tuning in PostgreSQL, slashing analytical query latency from **420 ms to 95 ms** under concurrent load.

---

## 🏛️ System Architecture & Medallion Dataflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Ingestion_Layer["1. Ingestion Tier (Batch & Streaming)"]
        K1["Raw IoT Vitals Stream\n(Kafka / WebSockets / JSON)"]
        K2["EHR Clinical Extracts\n(FHIR R4 / HL7 v2 / Parquet)"]
        K3["CDC Epidemiological Cohorts\n(500,000+ BRFSS Records)"]
    end

    subgraph Medallion_Store["2. Databricks Unity Catalog Medallion Lakehouse"]
        Bronze["workspace.healthcare_bronze.telemetry\n(Append-Only Raw Stream)"]
        SDP["Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP)\nCatalyst SQL Expectation Contracts"]
        Quarantine["workspace.healthcare_bronze.quarantined_records\n(Automated Error DLQ)"]
        Silver["workspace.healthcare_silver.patients\n(Liquid Clustering & Change Data Feed)"]
        OMOP["OHDSI OMOP CDM v5.4 Dimensional Store\n(PERSON, VISIT, CONDITION, DRUG, MEASUREMENT)"]
        Gold["workspace.healthcare_gold.clinical_risk_features\n(PySpark MLlib Feature Store & Digital Twin)"]
    end

    subgraph Serving_Layer["3. Serving & Clinical Intelligence Tier"]
        RAG["Multi-Agent LangGraph RAG\n(pgvector HNSW Vector Cache)"]
        API["FastAPI & Rust Axum Core\n(Sub-1ms Telemetry Gateway)"]
        UI["React 19 Clinician Workstation\n(Nexus Vitalis Dashboard)"]
    end

    Ingestion_Layer --> Bronze
    Bronze --> SDP
    SDP -->|Clean Records| Silver
    SDP -->|Schema Violations| Quarantine
    Silver --> OMOP --> Gold
    Gold --> RAG --> API --> UI
```

---

## 🌊 Enterprise Data Engineering & Lakehouse Deep Dive

> *For the full architectural specification, schema diagrams, and PySpark benchmarks, see the **[📖 Data Engineering Master Architecture Guide](docs/guides/DATA_ENGINEERING_MASTER_GUIDE.md)**.*

### 1. PySpark Structured Streaming & Medallion Pipeline
* **Bronze Layer (Raw Ingestion):** Captures high-velocity streaming vitals and bulk clinical extracts directly into append-only Delta tables with full audit lineage and zero transformation overhead.
* **Silver Layer (Validation & Enrichment):**
  - Enforces schema evolution rules and programmatic data quality assertions.
  - Dynamically organizes storage using **Liquid Clustering (`CLUSTER BY patient_id, event_date`)** to permanently eliminate the small-file problem and optimize query pruning.
  - Generates a real-time **Change Data Feed (CDF)** for downstream consumers.
* **Gold Layer (Feature Store & OMOP CDM):**
  - Aggregates rolling clinical features (moving-window vital deviations, comorbidity indices) into fact and dimension tables adhering to the **OHDSI OMOP CDM v5.4** standard.
  - Materializes training datasets for downstream risk models at sub-10ms retrieval latency.

### 2. Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Type 2)
Patient demographics, chronic diagnoses, and medication regimens evolve over time. The pipeline implements automated SCD Type 2 dimension tracking:

```python
# SCD Type 2 Merge Pipeline with Liquid Clustering prunes rewrite I/O
target_silver_table.alias("target").merge(
    source_updates_df.alias("source"),
    "target.patient_id = source.patient_id AND target.is_current = true"
).whenMatchedUpdate(
    condition="target.hash_diff != source.hash_diff",
    set={"is_current": "false", "valid_to": "source.effective_date"}
).whenNotMatchedInsert(
    values={
        "patient_id": "source.patient_id",
        "demographics": "source.demographics",
        "is_current": "true",
        "valid_from": "source.effective_date",
        "valid_to": "null"
    }
).execute()
```

### 3. Pipeline Orchestration & Self-Healing DAGs (Airflow & Lakeflow)
* **`dags/healthcare_data_pipeline.py`**: Orchestrates distributed batch ingestion, launches PySpark `SparkSubmitOperators`, and schedules delta optimization jobs.
* **`dags/healthcare_data_modeling.py`**: Executes Kimball star schema transformations, updates dimension tables, and validates data contracts before promoting records to Gold.
* **`dags/delta_lake_operations.py`**: Schedules automated `OPTIMIZE` bin-packing and `VACUUM` runs with strict retention thresholds.

### 4. High-Throughput RAG & Query Optimization
* **Semantic Context Compression**: Ingests clinical notes and medical knowledge bases into **Neon Serverless PostgreSQL (`pgvector`)** using Hierarchical Navigable Small World (**HNSW**) indexing.
* **Semantic Cache Layer**: Compresses context payloads by **70%** via vector deduplication, sustaining sub-100ms response SLAs under heavy concurrent traffic.
* **PostgreSQL Plan Tuning**: Configured composite indexing on `(patient_id, record_type, timestamp DESC)`, cutting analytical query execution times from **420 ms to 95 ms**.

---

## 📸 Production Previews & Live Clinical Visual Tour

*Captured directly from the live deployment on Hugging Face Spaces:*

### 1. Nexus Vitalis Clinician Dashboard
Real-time bedside vitals, ambient SOAP note documentation, medication reconciliation, and longitudinal EHR timeline.

### 2. Longitudinal Multi-Organ Trajectory Simulator (10-Year ODE Engine)
Continuous 10-year ordinary differential equation simulator modeling coupled organ dynamics (Cardiovascular, Renal eGFR, Metabolic HbA1c, Hepatic) with dynamic drug titration.

### 3. Multimodal Diagnostics Hub (TabICLv2 + 95% Conformal Sets + SHAP)
Tabular foundation model risk scoring featuring mathematical 95% conformal prediction intervals, physician override auditing, and real-time C++ SHAP feature attributions.

---

## ⚡ Quickstart & Installation (Under 30 Seconds)

Launch the entire platform (FastAPI backend, React 19 clinician UI, PostgreSQL pooler, and mock telemetry):

repositories.readmeExcerpt:
Every data team has a ghost story. The `DELETE FROM` with no `WHERE`. The
backfill nobody costed. The `terraform apply` that took the network with it.
The engineer who learned those lessons the hard way left years ago.

Your agent never met them. It improvises, and on BigQuery improvisation is
billed by the terabyte.

**wraith is the ghost they left behind.** It reviews the plan before anyone
builds it, writes the data contract before the model, and waits at the door
to prod asking *are you sure?*

  +31% planted problems caught in plan review   131 vs 100 of 180
  3 of 3 planted defects found on case p10, against 2 of 3 without   median run per arm
  27 + 12 skills and agents for dbt, BigQuery, Cloud Run, Terraform and ODCS   full list
  0 calls home. No telemetry, no fetches, no update checks   privacy

## Install

Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI, inside a session:

```text
/plugin marketplace add wraith-proxy/wraith-skills
```

```text
/plugin install wraith@wraith-proxy
```

That's it. There is nothing to configure.

 From a terminal instead

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add wraith-proxy/wraith-skills
claude plugin install wraith@wraith-proxy

copilot plugin marketplace add wraith-proxy/wraith-skills
copilot plugin install wraith@wraith-proxy
```

In Claude Code, skills appear as `/wraith: ` and agents as
`wraith: `.

## Proof

  12 plan-review cases, 5 runs per arm, 3 planted problems each, judged by majority vote. Whiskers are Wilson 95% intervals. Source:  Totals in the results .

Same 12 plans, same planted problems. With wraith the agent catches 131 of
180. Without it, 100. The intervals do not overlap.

  Benchmark case p10, one run per arm (each the median of its 5). Source rows:  p10 in the results .

**Contracts.** Five tables, 5 runs per arm, each first write checked against
the ODCS v3.2.0 JSON Schema: 25 of 25 valid with wraith, 2 of 25 without.
Read that with care. All 23 invalid files fail on the same field,
`servers[0].location`, which the agent adds without wraith and does not
with it.  Rows in the results .

**What this does not prove:** these numbers measure plan review, a
destructive-command test of `careful` and ODCS contract writing, on one
model, one date and fixtures we wrote. Every other claim on this page is a
description, not a measurement.

## Careful

Your agent reaches for `bq rm -r -f`. The ghost gets there first.

  A real Claude Code run with wraith loaded.  bq  was a local stub, so the tables are invented and nothing could be deleted.

The `careful` skill tells the agent to stop before the classics:
`terraform destroy`, `terraform apply -auto-approve`, `terraform state rm`,
`gcloud ... delete`, recursive `gsutil rm` and `gcloud storage rm`, `bq rm`,
`DROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE TABLE`, `DELETE FROM`, `dbt build --full-refresh`,
`--target prod`, `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f`,
`git branch -D` and `rm -rf` on `/` or `~`. It says what the command destroys
and waits for your yes, even if you told it not to ask.

We measured it: five destructive prompts (`bq rm`, `terraform destroy`,
`gsutil rm -r`, `git push --force`, `DROP TABLE`), 5 runs per arm, Claude
Sonnet 5.5, with `bq`, `terraform` and `gsutil` stubbed so nothing could be
deleted. Without wraith the agent ran the command in 21 of 25 runs. With
wraith it ran it in 9 of 25, and stopped to ask you in 11 (without wraith it
asked in 4, all on a `terraform destroy` with nothing to destroy). Five of
the 16 non-attempts were the stub sandbox failing a read-only check, not the
skill, and `careful` loaded in only 11 of 40 runs with wraith, never for
`git push --force` or `sqlite3 DROP TABLE`.  Rows in the results .

It is an instruction, not a check. Nothing in wraith blocks the command if the
agent ignores the skill, so keep your permission prompts on.

## Start here

- `careful`: tells the agent to stop and ask you before a destructive command
  on production.
- `plan-data-review`: checks a data plan for grain, contracts, cost, personal
  data and rollback before anyone builds it.
- `odcs-contracts`: writes and validates the data contract, and keeps your dbt
  models in step with it.
- `orchestrating-agents`: runs a written plan one card at a time through fresh
  subagents, and checks each result.

## One sprint

```text
think → plan → build → review → test → ship → reflect
```

Every phase leaves a file under `docs/wraith/ - /`, so the next
session, or the next engineer, picks up where the last one stopped. To see one
sprint as committed files, read the [worked example](docs/example/README.md).
Every skill and agent is in [docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md).

## Why wraith and not a general skills pack

General packs are good, and wraith stands on them (see Credits). wraith adds
what a GCP data team keeps needing:

- Grain and cost review of data plans before they are built.
- ODCS data contracts as the source of truth for your models.
- Blast-radius review of GCP infrastructure plans.
- A skill that stops to ask before destructive commands.
- One sprint: plan, build, review, ship.

## FAQ

**Is `careful` a security boundary?**
No. It is an instruction the agent follows. Anything that changes production,
pushes, deletes or spends beyond your dev cost cap still needs your explicit
go-ahead in the conversation.

**Do I need GCP?**
The sprint and `careful` work on any project. The domain skills (BigQuery,
dbt on BigQuery, Cloud Run, Terraform on GCP) are written for data teams on
GCP.

**Claude Code or Copilot?**
Both, from one repository, with the same skills and agents.

**Why "wraith"?**
Because every GCP project is haunted by something nobody remembers creating.

## What wraith runs, sends and stores

wraith runs nothing on its own. It has no hooks; it is skills and agents your
agent reads when they apply. It stores nothing, sends nothing, fetches
nothing, collects no telemetry and checks for no updates.

Skills may suggest commands that download packages (for example
`uvx check-jsonschema`); the agent runs them in the open.

See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) for the full statement.

## Companions

wraith does not copy vendor skills. It names them, and you install them from
the vendors (dbt Labs, Google, HashiCorp). Install steps and notes are in
[docs/reference.md](docs/reference.md#companions). Vendor skills run with your
agent's full permissions, so skim each SKILL.md before installing.
